questions.question: Let [latex]f(x)=xe^{-x}[/latex]. The maximum value of the function in the interval [latex](0,\infty )[/latex] is
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} f(x)&=xe^{-x}\\ f'(x)&=e^{-x}-xe^{-x}=0\\ e^{-x}(1-x)&=0\\ x&=1\\ f''(x)&=-e^{-x}-e^{-x}+xe^{-x}\\ &=e^{-x}(x-2)\\ f''(1)&=e^{-1}(-1)=-e^{-1} \lt 0 \end{aligned}[/latex] Hence f(x) has maximum value at x=1 [latex]f(1)=1\cdot e^{-1}=e^{-1}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{aligned} f(x)&=xe^{-x}\\ f'(x)&=e^{-x}-xe^{-x}=0\\ e^{-x}(1-x)&=0\\ x&=1\\ f''(x)&=-e^{-x}-e^{-x}+xe^{-x}\\ &=e^{-x}(x-2)\\ f''(1)&=e^{-1}(-1)=-e^{-1} \lt 0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Hence f(x) has maximum value at x=1
[latex]f(1)=1\cdot e^{-1}=e^{-1}[/latex]

questions.question: The line integral of function F=yzi, in the counterclockwise direction, along the circle [latex]x^{2}+y^{2}=1[/latex] at z=1 is
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} \bar{F} &=yz\hat{i} \\ \bigtriangledown \times \bar{F} &=\begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k}\\ \frac{\partial }{\partial x} & \frac{\partial }{\partial y} &\frac{\partial }{\partial z} \\ yz& 0 & 0 \end{vmatrix} \\ &= \hat{i}(0)-\hat{j}(0-y)+\hat{k}(0-z)\\ &=0\hat{i}+y\hat{j}-z\hat{k} \end{aligned}[/latex] By strokes theoram, [latex]\begin{aligned} \int _C\bar{F}\cdot d\bar{r}&=\int _S (\bigtriangledown \times \bar{F})\cdot \hat{n}ds\\ &=\int _S (y\hat{j}-z\hat{k})\cdot \hat{k}ds\\ &=\int _S -z \; ds \;\;\;\text{ Since }\; z=1\\ &=\int _S -1 \; ds=(-1)S=(-1)\pi =-\pi \end{aligned}[/latex] where S is surface area of [latex]x^2+y^2=1[/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\;S=\pi(1)^2=\pi[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \bar{F} &=yz\hat{i} \\ \bigtriangledown \times \bar{F} &=\begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k}\\ \frac{\partial }{\partial x} & \frac{\partial }{\partial y} &\frac{\partial }{\partial z} \\ yz& 0 & 0 \end{vmatrix} \\ &= \hat{i}(0)-\hat{j}(0-y)+\hat{k}(0-z)\\ &=0\hat{i}+y\hat{j}-z\hat{k} \end{aligned}[/latex]
By strokes theoram,
[latex]\begin{aligned} \int _C\bar{F}\cdot d\bar{r}&=\int _S (\bigtriangledown \times \bar{F})\cdot \hat{n}ds\\ &=\int _S (y\hat{j}-z\hat{k})\cdot \hat{k}ds\\ &=\int _S -z \; ds \;\;\;\text{ Since }\; z=1\\ &=\int _S -1 \; ds=(-1)S=(-1)\pi =-\pi \end{aligned}[/latex]
where S is surface area of [latex]x^2+y^2=1[/latex]
[latex]\therefore \;\;S=\pi(1)^2=\pi[/latex]

questions.question:
A system matrix is given as follows [latex]A=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & -1\\ -6& -11&6 \\ -6 & -11 & 5 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] The absolute value of the ratio of the maximum eigenvalue to the minimum
eigenvalue is _______.
questions.explanation: Characteristic equation [latex]|A-\lambda I|=0[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} \begin{vmatrix} -\lambda & 1 & -1\\ -6 & -11-\lambda & 6\\ -6&-11 & 5-\lambda \end{vmatrix} = 0\\ \Rightarrow \; -\lambda [-55+11\lambda -5\lambda +\lambda ^2+66] \\ -1[-30+6\lambda +36]-1[66-66-6\lambda ]=0 \\ \Rightarrow \; -\lambda (\lambda ^2+6\lambda +11)-1(6\lambda +6)+6\lambda =0 \\ \Rightarrow \;-\lambda ^3-6\lambda ^2-11\lambda -6=0 \\ \Rightarrow \;\lambda ^3+6\lambda ^2+11\lambda +6=0 \\ \Rightarrow \; (\lambda +1)(\lambda +2)(\lambda +3)=0 \\ \Rightarrow \;\lambda =-1,-2,-3 \end{aligned}[/latex] The absolute values of [latex]\lambda[/latex] are [latex]|\lambda |=1,2,3[/latex] Ratio of maximum and minimum eigen value is [latex]=3:1=\frac{3}{1}=3[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Characteristic equation [latex]|A-\lambda I|=0[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \begin{vmatrix} -\lambda & 1 & -1\\ -6 & -11-\lambda & 6\\ -6&-11 & 5-\lambda \end{vmatrix} = 0\\ \Rightarrow \; -\lambda [-55+11\lambda -5\lambda +\lambda ^2+66] \\ -1[-30+6\lambda +36]-1[66-66-6\lambda ]=0 \\ \Rightarrow \; -\lambda (\lambda ^2+6\lambda +11)-1(6\lambda +6)+6\lambda =0 \\ \Rightarrow \;-\lambda ^3-6\lambda ^2-11\lambda -6=0 \\ \Rightarrow \;\lambda ^3+6\lambda ^2+11\lambda +6=0 \\ \Rightarrow \; (\lambda +1)(\lambda +2)(\lambda +3)=0 \\ \Rightarrow \;\lambda =-1,-2,-3 \end{aligned}[/latex]
The absolute values of [latex]\lambda[/latex] are [latex]|\lambda |=1,2,3[/latex]
Ratio of maximum and minimum eigen value is [latex]=3:1=\frac{3}{1}=3[/latex]

questions.question: Consider the differential equation [latex]x^{2}\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}+x\frac{dy}{dx}-y=0[/latex]. Which of the following is a solution to this differential equation for [latex]x \gt 0[/latex] ?
questions.explanation:
[latex]\begin{aligned}
x^2\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}+x\frac{dy}{dx}-y&=0\\
\text{Let,  }x=e^z\leftrightarrow z&=\log x\\
s\frac{d}{dx}=xD=\theta &=\frac{d}{dz}\\
x^2D^2&=\theta (\theta -1)\\
(x^2D^2+xD-1)y&=0\\
[\theta (\theta -1)+\theta -1]y&=0\\
(\theta ^2-\theta +\theta -1)&=0\\
(\theta ^2-1)y&=0\\
\text{Auxiliary equation is }m^2-1&=0\\
m&=\pm 1\\
\text{CF is  }C_1e^{-z}+C_2e^z&\\
\text{Solution is   }y&=C_1e^{-z}+C_2e^z\\
y&=C_1x^{-1}+C_2x\\
y&=C_1\frac{1}{x}+C_2x
\end{aligned}[/latex] One independent solution is [latex]\frac{1}{x}[/latex] Another independent solution is x.
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{aligned} x^2\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}+x\frac{dy}{dx}-y&=0\\ \text{Let, }x=e^z\leftrightarrow z&=\log x\\ s\frac{d}{dx}=xD=\theta &=\frac{d}{dz}\\ x^2D^2&=\theta (\theta -1)\\ (x^2D^2+xD-1)y&=0\\ [\theta (\theta -1)+\theta -1]y&=0\\ (\theta ^2-\theta +\theta -1)&=0\\ (\theta ^2-1)y&=0\\ \text{Auxiliary equation is }m^2-1&=0\\ m&=\pm 1\\ \text{CF is }C_1e^{-z}+C_2e^z&\\ \text{Solution is }y&=C_1e^{-z}+C_2e^z\\ y&=C_1x^{-1}+C_2x\\ y&=C_1\frac{1}{x}+C_2x \end{aligned}[/latex]
One independent solution is [latex]\frac{1}{x}[/latex]
Another independent solution is x.

questions.question: To evaluate the double integral [latex]\int_{0}^{8}(\int_{y/2}^{(y/2)+1}(\frac{2x-y}{2})dx)dy[/latex], we make the substitution [latex]u=(\frac{2x-y}{2})[/latex] and v=y/2 . The integral will reduce to
questions.explanation: [latex]\int_{0}^{8}\left ( \int_{y/2}^{(y/2)+1} \left ( \frac{2x-y}{2} \right )dx\right ) dy[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{2x-y}{2} &=u \\ x-\frac{y}{2}&=u \\ dx&= du\\ \text{at }x &=\frac{y}{2} \\ u&=\frac{\frac{2y}{2}-y}{2}=0 \\ \text{at }x &=\frac{y}{2}+1 \\ u &=\frac{2\left ( \frac{y}{2}+1 \right )-y}{2}\\ &=\frac{y+2-y}{2}=1 \end{aligned}[/latex] Thus, integral becomes [latex]\int_{0}^{8}\left (\int_{0}^{1} u du \right )dy[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} v&=\frac{y}{2} \\ dv&=\frac{dy}{2} \\ y=0&= \\ \Rightarrow \;\; v &= 0\\ &y=8 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; v &= 4\\ &\;\;=\int_{0}^{4}\left ( \int_{0}^{1} udu\right )\times 2dv\\ &\;\;= \int_{0}^{4}\left ( \int_{0}^{1} 2udu\right )\times dv \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\int_{0}^{8}\left ( \int_{y/2}^{(y/2)+1} \left ( \frac{2x-y}{2} \right )dx\right ) dy[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{2x-y}{2} &=u \\ x-\frac{y}{2}&=u \\ dx&= du\\ \text{at }x &=\frac{y}{2} \\ u&=\frac{\frac{2y}{2}-y}{2}=0 \\ \text{at }x &=\frac{y}{2}+1 \\ u &=\frac{2\left ( \frac{y}{2}+1 \right )-y}{2}\\ &=\frac{y+2-y}{2}=1 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Thus, integral becomes [latex]\int_{0}^{8}\left (\int_{0}^{1} u du \right )dy[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} v&=\frac{y}{2} \\ dv&=\frac{dy}{2} \\ y=0&= \\ \Rightarrow \;\; v &= 0\\ &y=8 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; v &= 4\\ &\;\;=\int_{0}^{4}\left ( \int_{0}^{1} udu\right )\times 2dv\\ &\;\;= \int_{0}^{4}\left ( \int_{0}^{1} 2udu\right )\times dv \end{aligned}[/latex]

Critical points are [-3,-2,3]

questions.question: Two matrices A and B are given below: [latex]A=\begin{bmatrix} p &q \\ r& s \end{bmatrix};[/latex]  [latex]B=\begin{bmatrix} p^2+q^2 & pr +qs \\ pr+qs & r^2+s^2 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] If the rank of matrix A is N, then the rank of matrix B is
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} A &=\begin{bmatrix} p & q\\ r & s \end{bmatrix} \\ A \times A=A^2&=\begin{bmatrix} p^2+q^2 & pr+qs\\ pr+qs & r^2+s^2 \end{bmatrix} =B \\ A^2 &=B \end{aligned}[/latex] Rank of amtrix does not change when we squaring the matrix, hence rank of B = rank of A=N.
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{aligned} A &=\begin{bmatrix} p & q\\ r & s \end{bmatrix} \\ A \times A=A^2&=\begin{bmatrix} p^2+q^2 & pr+qs\\ pr+qs & r^2+s^2 \end{bmatrix} =B \\ A^2 &=B \end{aligned}[/latex]
Rank of amtrix does not change when we squaring the matrix, hence rank of B = rank of A=N.

questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} \vec{V}&=y\hat{i}+z\hat{j}+x\hat{k}\\ \hat{i}\frac{\partial (fV)}{\partial x}+\hat{j}\frac{\partial (fV)}{\partial y}+\hat{k}\frac{\partial (fV)}{\partial z}&=x^2y+y^2z+z^2x\\ y\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}+z\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}+x\frac{\partial f}{\partial z}&=x^2y+y^2z+z^2x\;\;...(i)\\ \vec{V}\cdot \Delta f&=y\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}+z\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}+x\frac{\partial f}{\partial z}\;\;...(ii)\\ \text{From equations (i) and (ii)}\\ \vec{V}\cdot \Delta f&=x^2y+y^2z+z^2x \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.explanation: Given, [latex]f(x)=e^x-1[/latex] or, [latex]f(x_K)=e^{x_K}-1[/latex] and [latex]x_0=1[/latex] In Newton-Raphson method, we have [latex]\begin{aligned} x_{K+1}&=\left [ x_K-\frac{f(x_K)}{f'(x_K)} \right ] \\ x_1&= \left [ x_0- \frac{f(x_0)}{f'(x_0)}\right ]\;\;...(i)\\ \text{Now, } f(x_0)&=e^{x_0}-1=e^1-1=(e-1) \\ \text{and, } f'(x)&=e6x \\ \therefore \;\; f'(x_0) &=e^1=e \end{aligned}[/latex] Putting the values, we get: [latex]\begin{aligned} x_1&=\left [ 1-\frac{e-1}{e} \right ]=\left [ \frac{e-e+1}{e} \right ]=e^{-1}\\ \text{Also, }x_2&=\left [ x_1-\frac{f(x_1)}{f'(x_1)} \right ]\;\;...(ii)\\ \text{Now, }x_1&=\frac{1}{e}=e^{-1} \text{ and } f(x_1)=(e^{e^{-1}}-1)\\ f'(x_1)&=e^{e^{-1}} \end{aligned}[/latex] Putting the value, we get: [latex]\begin{aligned} x_2&=\left [ e^{-1}-\frac{(e^{e^{-1}}-1)}{e^{e^{-1}}} \right ]\\ &=\left [ e^{-1}-\frac{(e^{0.37}-1)}{e^{0.37}} \right ]=0.06 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: [latex]C_0[/latex] is the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with air as dielectric (as in figure (a)). If, half of the entire gap as shown in figure (b) is filled with a dielectric of permittivity [latex]\epsilon _r[/latex] , the expression for the modified capacitance is
questions.explanation: Let A be the area of the parallel plate capacitor and d be the distance between the plates. Let [latex]C_1[/latex] be the capacitance of half portion with air as dielectic medium and [latex]C_2[/latex] be capacitance with a dielectic of permitivity, [latex]\varepsilon _r[/latex]. Then, [latex]C_1=\frac{\varepsilon _0 \left ( \frac{A}{2} \right )}{d}[/latex] (As area become half) and [latex]C_2=\frac{\varepsilon _0 \varepsilon _r \left ( \frac{A}{2} \right )}{d}[/latex] (As area becomes half) Now, these two capacitance will be in parallel if a voltage is applied between the plates as same potential difference will be there between both the capacitance. Equivalent capacitance is [latex]\begin{aligned} C_{eqv} &= C_1+C_2\\ &=\frac{\varepsilon _0 A}{2d}+ \frac{\varepsilon _0 \varepsilon _r A}{2d}\\ &= \frac{\varepsilon _0 A}{2d}(1+ \varepsilon _r)=\frac{C_0}{2}(1+\varepsilon _r) \end{aligned}[/latex] Therefore, modified capacitance, [latex]C_{eqv}=\frac{C_0}{2}(1+\varepsilon _r)[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Let A be the area of the parallel plate capacitor and d be the distance between the plates.

Let [latex]C_1[/latex] be the capacitance of half portion with air as dielectic medium and [latex]C_2[/latex] be capacitance with a dielectic of permitivity, [latex]\varepsilon _r[/latex].
Then, [latex]C_1=\frac{\varepsilon _0 \left ( \frac{A}{2} \right )}{d}[/latex] (As area become half)
and [latex]C_2=\frac{\varepsilon _0 \varepsilon _r \left ( \frac{A}{2} \right )}{d}[/latex] (As area becomes half)
Now, these two capacitance will be in parallel if a voltage is applied between the plates as same potential difference will be there between both the capacitance.

Equivalent capacitance is
[latex]\begin{aligned} C_{eqv} &= C_1+C_2\\ &=\frac{\varepsilon _0 A}{2d}+ \frac{\varepsilon _0 \varepsilon _r A}{2d}\\ &= \frac{\varepsilon _0 A}{2d}(1+ \varepsilon _r)=\frac{C_0}{2}(1+\varepsilon _r) \end{aligned}[/latex]
Therefore, modified capacitance,
[latex]C_{eqv}=\frac{C_0}{2}(1+\varepsilon _r)[/latex]

questions.question:
A star connected 400 V, 50 Hz, 4 pole synchronous machine gave the following
open circuit and short circuit test results : Open circuit test : [latex]V_{oc}[/latex] = 400 V (rms, line-to-line) at field current, [latex]I_{f}[/latex] = 2.3 A Short circuit test : [latex]I_{sc}[/latex]= 10 A (rms, phase) at field current,
[latex]I_{f}[/latex] = 1.5 A The value of per phase synchronous impedance in [latex]\Omega[/latex] at rated voltage is_____.
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Given, for}\;\;V_{OC} &= 400V(rms)\\ &= \frac{400}{\sqrt{3}}\\ &= 230.94 \;\text{(Phase value),}\\ I_f&= 2.3A\\ \text{for}\;\; I_{sc}&=10A \;\text{(rms, phase)} \\ I_f&= 1.5A\\ & \therefore \;\;\text{Base impedance}\\ Z_{base}&=\frac{V_{OC}}{I_{sc}}\\ &=\frac{230.94}{10}=23.094\Omega \end{aligned}[/latex] For finding the synchronous impedance at rated voltage, saturation effect of the machine has to be considered (i.e. the adjusted value of [latex]Z_s[/latex]) short circuit ratio, [latex]\begin{aligned} SCR &=\frac{I_f \;for \; V_{OC}}{I_f \;for \; I_{sc}} \\ &=\frac{1}{Z_{s_{(sat)pu}}} =\frac{2.3}{1.5}\\ Z_{s_{(sat)pu}} &= 0.65 pu \end{aligned}[/latex] Therefore, actual value of [latex]Z_s[/latex] at rated voltage [latex]\begin{aligned} &=Z_{s_{(sat)pu}} \times Z_{base} \\ &=0.65 \times 23.094=15.06\Omega \\ \therefore \;\;Z_s&= 15.06\Omega \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Given, for}\;\;V_{OC} &= 400V(rms)\\ &= \frac{400}{\sqrt{3}}\\ &= 230.94 \;\text{(Phase value),}\\ I_f&= 2.3A\\ \text{for}\;\; I_{sc}&=10A \;\text{(rms, phase)} \\ I_f&= 1.5A\\ & \therefore \;\;\text{Base impedance}\\ Z_{base}&=\frac{V_{OC}}{I_{sc}}\\ &=\frac{230.94}{10}=23.094\Omega \end{aligned}[/latex]
For finding the synchronous impedance at rated voltage, saturation effect of the machine has to be considered (i.e. the adjusted value of [latex]Z_s[/latex])
short circuit ratio,
[latex]\begin{aligned} SCR &=\frac{I_f \;for \; V_{OC}}{I_f \;for \; I_{sc}} \\ &=\frac{1}{Z_{s_{(sat)pu}}} =\frac{2.3}{1.5}\\ Z_{s_{(sat)pu}} &= 0.65 pu \end{aligned}[/latex]
Therefore, actual value of [latex]Z_s[/latex] at rated voltage
[latex]\begin{aligned} &=Z_{s_{(sat)pu}} \times Z_{base} \\ &=0.65 \times 23.094=15.06\Omega \\ \therefore \;\;Z_s&= 15.06\Omega \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.explanation: A CRO uses a horizontal input voltage which is an internally generated ramp voltage (i.e. linear sweep voltage) called "Time base of CRO". questions.question: In an unbalanced three phase system, phase current [latex]I_a = 1\angle -90^{\circ}[/latex] pu, negative sequence current [latex]I_{b2}=4 \angle( -150^{\circ})[/latex], zero sequence current [latex]I_{c0}=3 \angle -90^{\circ}[/latex] pu. The magnitude of phase current [latex]I_{b}[/latex]  in pu is
questions.explanation:
Given, [latex]\begin{aligned} I_a&= 1\angle (-90^{\circ})pu\\ I_b&= 4\angle (-150^{\circ})pu\\ I_c&= 3\angle (90^{\circ})pu \end{aligned}[/latex] As zero sequence current in all the three phases of unbalanced [latex]3-\phi[/latex] system are equal, therefore, [latex]I_{a_0}=I_{b_0}=I_{c_0}=3\angle 90^{\circ}pu[/latex] Also,  [latex]I_{b_2}=4\angle -150^{\circ}[/latex] =Negative phase sequence current of phase b. Therefore, referring to the negative phase sequence phasor, [latex]I_{b_2}=4\angle (-150^{\circ}-120^{\circ})=4\angle-270^{\circ}pu[/latex] We know that, phase current vectors in matrix form are given by [latex] \begin{aligned}
\begin{bmatrix}
I_a\\ 
I_b\\ 
I_c
\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}
1 &1  &1 \\ 
 1& a^2 &a \\ 
1 & a &a^2 
\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}
I_{a_0}\\ 
I_{a_1}\\ 
I_{a_2}
\end{bmatrix} \\ 
\text{Here, } I_a&=I_{a_0}+I_{a_1}+I_{a_2} \\ 
\text{Given, } I_a&=1\angle -90^{\circ} \\ 
 I_{a_0}&=3\angle 90^{\circ} \\ 
 I_{a_2}&=4\angle -270^{\circ} \\ 
 \text{Therefore,}& \\ 
 I_{a_1}&=I_a-(I_{a_0}+I_{a_2}) \\ 
 &=(1\angle -90^{\circ})-(3\angle 90^{\circ}+4\angle 270^{\circ}) \\ 
 I_{a_1}&=8\angle -90^{\circ}pu \\ 
 \text{Therefore,}& \\
 I_b&=I_{a_0}+a^2I_{a_1}+aI_{a_2}\\
&=(3\angle 90^{\circ})+(1\angle 120^{\circ})^2 (8\angle -90^{\circ}) \\
&+(1\angle 120^{\circ})(4\angle -270^{\circ})\\
&=3\angle 90^{\circ}+8\angle 150^{\circ}+4\angle -150^{\circ}\\
I_b&=11.53\angle 154.3^{\circ}pu\\
&\text{Magnitude of phase current,}\\
I_b&=11.53\;pu
\end{aligned}[/latex]

Given,
[latex]\begin{aligned} I_a&= 1\angle (-90^{\circ})pu\\ I_b&= 4\angle (-150^{\circ})pu\\ I_c&= 3\angle (90^{\circ})pu \end{aligned}[/latex]
As zero sequence current in all the three phases of unbalanced [latex]3-\phi[/latex] system are equal, therefore,

Also, [latex]I_{b_2}=4\angle -150^{\circ}[/latex]

questions.explanation: Given, at 230V, 50 Hz, core loss =1050 W and at 138 V, 30 Hz, core loss =500 W Let, [latex]V_1=230 V, \;f_1=50Hz[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Eddy current loss} &=P_{e1} \\ \text{Hysteresis loss}&=P_{h1} \\ V_2=138V &, f_230Hz \\ \text{Eddy current loss} &=P_{e2} \\ \text{Hysteresis loss}&=P_{h2} \\ \text{we know that, } & \\ \text{Eddy current loss,}\;& P_e \propto B_m^2f^2 \\ \text{and hysteresis loss,}&P_h \propto B_m^xf\propto B_m^1.6 f \\ &(\text{Typical value of x=1.6}) \end{aligned}[/latex] The transformer induced emf equation is: [latex]\begin{aligned} V_1 &=\sqrt{2} \pi \phi _m N \\ V_1&= \sqrt{2} \pi f B_m A N\\ \text{where,}\;\; \frac{V}{t} &=\text{constant} \end{aligned}[/latex] i.e. flux = constant ( to avoid over fluxing) [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Eddy current loss,} &P_e \propto V^2 \\ \text{and hysteresis loss,}&P_h \propto\frac{V^{1.6}}{f^{0.6}} \end{aligned}[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{P_{e2}}{P_{e1}} &=\left ( \frac{V_2}{V_1} \right )^2=\left ( \frac{138}{230} \right )^2=0.36 \\ \text{or,} \;\; P_{e2} &= 0.36P_{e1}\;\;...(i)\\ \text{Also,} \;\;\frac{P_{h2}}{P_{e1}} &=\left ( \frac{V_2}{V_1} \right )^{1.6} \times \left ( \frac{f_1}{f_2} \right )^{0.6}\\ &=\left ( \frac{138}{230} \right )^{1.6} \times \left ( \frac{50}{30} \right )^{0.6} \\ &= (0.6)^{1.6} \times \frac{1}{(0.6)^{0.6}}=0.6\\ \therefore \;\; P_{h2} &=0.6P_{h1} \;\;...(ii) \end{aligned} [/latex] Given at 230V, 50Hz [latex]\text{Core loss}=P_{e1}+P_{h1}=1050W\;\;...(iii) [/latex] At 138V, 30Hz, [latex]\text{Core loss}=P_{e2}+P_{h2}=500W [/latex] or,   [latex]0.36P_{e1}+0.6P_{h1}=500W\;\;...(iv)[/latex] solving equation (iii) and (iv), we get [latex]P_{h1}=508W [/latex] and [latex] P_{e1}=542W[/latex] Therefore, hysteresis and eddy current losses at 230V, 50Hz are 508W and 542W respectively.
questions.explanation_html:
Given, at 230V, 50 Hz, core loss =1050 W
and at 138 V, 30 Hz, core loss =500 W
Let, [latex]V_1=230 V, \;f_1=50Hz[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Eddy current loss} &=P_{e1} \\ \text{Hysteresis loss}&=P_{h1} \\ V_2=138V &, f_230Hz \\ \text{Eddy current loss} &=P_{e2} \\ \text{Hysteresis loss}&=P_{h2} \\ \text{we know that, } & \\ \text{Eddy current loss,}\;& P_e \propto B_m^2f^2 \\ \text{and hysteresis loss,}&P_h \propto B_m^xf\propto B_m^1.6 f \\ &(\text{Typical value of x=1.6}) \end{aligned}[/latex]
The transformer induced emf equation is:
[latex]\begin{aligned} V_1 &=\sqrt{2} \pi \phi _m N \\ V_1&= \sqrt{2} \pi f B_m A N\\ \text{where,}\;\; \frac{V}{t} &=\text{constant} \end{aligned}[/latex]
i.e. flux = constant ( to avoid over fluxing)
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Eddy current loss,} &P_e \propto V^2 \\ \text{and hysteresis loss,}&P_h \propto\frac{V^{1.6}}{f^{0.6}} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{P_{e2}}{P_{e1}} &=\left ( \frac{V_2}{V_1} \right )^2=\left ( \frac{138}{230} \right )^2=0.36 \\ \text{or,} \;\; P_{e2} &= 0.36P_{e1}\;\;...(i)\\ \text{Also,} \;\;\frac{P_{h2}}{P_{e1}} &=\left ( \frac{V_2}{V_1} \right )^{1.6} \times \left ( \frac{f_1}{f_2} \right )^{0.6}\\ &=\left ( \frac{138}{230} \right )^{1.6} \times \left ( \frac{50}{30} \right )^{0.6} \\ &= (0.6)^{1.6} \times \frac{1}{(0.6)^{0.6}}=0.6\\ \therefore \;\; P_{h2} &=0.6P_{h1} \;\;...(ii) \end{aligned} [/latex]
Given at 230V, 50Hz
[latex]\text{Core loss}=P_{e1}+P_{h1}=1050W\;\;...(iii) [/latex]
At 138V, 30Hz,
[latex]\text{Core loss}=P_{e2}+P_{h2}=500W [/latex]
or, [latex]0.36P_{e1}+0.6P_{h1}=500W\;\;...(iv)[/latex]
solving equation (iii) and (iv), we get
[latex]P_{h1}=508W [/latex] and [latex] P_{e1}=542W[/latex]
Therefore, hysteresis and eddy current losses at 230V, 50Hz are 508W and 542W respectively.

questions.question: A 15 kW, 230 V dc shunt motor has armature circuit resistance of 0.4 [latex]\Omega[/latex] and field circuit resistance of 230 [latex]\Omega[/latex] . At no load and rated voltage, the motor runs at 1400 rpm and the line current drawn by the motor is 5 A. At full load, the motor draws a line current of 70 A. Neglect armature reaction. The full load speed of the motor in rpm is_____.
questions.explanation: Given, [latex]R_a=0.4\Omega , [/latex] [latex]R_f=230\Omega , [/latex]  [latex]V=230 \;\text{volt} [/latex] At no load, speed, [latex]N_0=1400 \;\text{rpm}, [/latex]  [latex]I_{L_0}=5A [/latex] Field current,  [latex]I_f=\frac{V}{R_f}=\frac{230}{230}=1A[/latex] No load armature current, [latex]I_{a_0}=5-1=4A[/latex] Induced emf at no-load, [latex]E_{a_0}=V-I_{a_0}R_a[/latex] [latex]\;\; \;\;=230-4 \times 0.4=228.4 V [/latex] Also, at full load, [latex]I_{L_{fl}}=70A [/latex] [latex]I_{a_{fl}}=I_{L_{fl}}-I_f=70-1=69A [/latex] Induced emf at full load, [latex]E_{a_{fl}}=V-I_{a{fl}}R_a [/latex] [latex]E_{a_{fl}}=230 -69 \times 0.4=202.4V [/latex] we know that, [latex]\begin{aligned} E_a&\propto \phi \omega _m \alpha \propto N \\ E_a &\propto N \\ (\text{as flux} \; \phi \; &\text{is constant in shunt motor}) \\ \therefore \; \frac{E_{a_{fl}}}{E_{a_{0}}} &=\frac{N_{fl}}{N_0} \\ N_{fl}&= \frac{E_{a_{fl}}}{E_{a_{0}}} \times N_0 \\ &=\left ( \frac{202.4}{228.4} \right ) \times 1400 \end{aligned}[/latex] Therefore, full-load speed of motor = 1240.63 rpm

Given, [latex]R_a=0.4\Omega , [/latex] [latex]R_f=230\Omega , [/latex] [latex]V=230 \;\text{volt} [/latex]
At no load, speed, [latex]N_0=1400 \;\text{rpm}, [/latex] [latex]I_{L_0}=5A [/latex]
Field current, [latex]I_f=\frac{V}{R_f}=\frac{230}{230}=1A[/latex]

No load armature current, [latex]I_{a_0}=5-1=4A[/latex]
Induced emf at no-load,
[latex]E_{a_0}=V-I_{a_0}R_a[/latex]
[latex]\;\; \;\;=230-4 \times 0.4=228.4 V [/latex]
Also, at full load,
[latex]I_{L_{fl}}=70A [/latex]
[latex]I_{a_{fl}}=I_{L_{fl}}-I_f=70-1=69A [/latex]
Induced emf at full load,
[latex]E_{a_{fl}}=V-I_{a{fl}}R_a [/latex]
[latex]E_{a_{fl}}=230 -69 \times 0.4=202.4V [/latex]
we know that,
[latex]\begin{aligned} E_a&\propto \phi \omega _m \alpha \propto N \\ E_a &\propto N \\ (\text{as flux} \; \phi \; &\text{is constant in shunt motor}) \\ \therefore \; \frac{E_{a_{fl}}}{E_{a_{0}}} &=\frac{N_{fl}}{N_0} \\ N_{fl}&= \frac{E_{a_{fl}}}{E_{a_{0}}} \times N_0 \\ &=\left ( \frac{202.4}{228.4} \right ) \times 1400 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Therefore, full-load speed of motor = 1240.63 rpm

questions.question: A 3 phase, 50 Hz, six pole induction motor has a rotor resistance of 0.1[latex]\Omega[/latex] and reactance of 0.92[latex]\Omega[/latex] . Neglect the voltage drop in stator and assume that the rotor resistance is constant. Given that the full load slip is 3%, the ratio of maximum torque to full load torque is
questions.explanation: Given, [latex]\begin{aligned} R'_2 &=0.1\Omega \\ X'_2&= 0.92\Omega \\ S_{fl}&=3\%=0.03 \end{aligned}[/latex] Slip at maximum torque, [latex] S_m=\frac{R'_2}{X'_2}=\frac{0.1}{0.92}=0.1087 [/latex] We know that, [latex]\begin{aligned}\frac{T_{fl}}{T_{em}}&=\frac{2}{\left ( \frac{S_m}{S_{fl}}+\frac{S_{fl}}{S_m} \right )}\\ \therefore \;\; \frac{T_{fl}}{T_{em}}&=\frac{2}{\left ( \frac{0.1087}{0.03}+\frac{0.03}{0.1087} \right )}\\ &=\frac{2}{3.623+0.275}=\frac{2}{3.898}\\ \frac{T_{em}}{T_{fl}}&= 1.949 \end{aligned}[/latex] Therefore, ratio of maximum torque to full-load torque [latex]=\frac{T_{em}}{T_{fl}}= 1.949[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Given,
[latex]\begin{aligned} R'_2 &=0.1\Omega \\ X'_2&= 0.92\Omega \\ S_{fl}&=3\%=0.03 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Slip at maximum torque,
[latex] S_m=\frac{R'_2}{X'_2}=\frac{0.1}{0.92}=0.1087 [/latex]
We know that,
[latex]\begin{aligned}\frac{T_{fl}}{T_{em}}&=\frac{2}{\left ( \frac{S_m}{S_{fl}}+\frac{S_{fl}}{S_m} \right )}\\ \therefore \;\; \frac{T_{fl}}{T_{em}}&=\frac{2}{\left ( \frac{0.1087}{0.03}+\frac{0.03}{0.1087} \right )}\\ &=\frac{2}{3.623+0.275}=\frac{2}{3.898}\\ \frac{T_{em}}{T_{fl}}&= 1.949 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Therefore, ratio of maximum torque to full-load torque [latex]=\frac{T_{em}}{T_{fl}}= 1.949[/latex]

questions.question: A distribution feeder of 1 km length having resistance, but negligible reactance, is fed from both the ends by 400 V, 50 Hz balanced sources. Both voltage sources [latex]S_1 \; and \; S_2[/latex] are in phase. The feeder supplies concentrated loads of unity power factor as shown in the figure. The contributions of [latex]S_1 \; and \; S_2[/latex] in 100 A current supplied at location P respectively, are
questions.explanation:
Let the resistance of whole length of feeder be [latex]R\;\Omega[/latex], length of feeder =1000m. [latex]\therefore \;[/latex] Resistance per unit length [latex]=\frac{R}{1000}\Omega /meter[/latex] [latex]\therefore \;[/latex] Resistance of 400 m length [latex]=\frac{R}{1000} \times 400 =\frac{2R}{5} \Omega [/latex] [latex]\therefore \;[/latex] Resistance of 200 m length [latex] =\frac{R}{5} \Omega [/latex] Let the current supplied by the sources be [latex]I_1 \text{ and } I_2[/latex]. Applying KVL from source [latex]S_1 \text{ and } S_2[/latex], we have: [latex]\begin{aligned}
400 &= \frac{2R}{5}I_1+\frac{R}{5}(I_1-200)\\ & -\frac{R}{5}(I_2-200)-\frac{R}{5}I_2+400\\ 
 0&= \frac{2}{5}I_1 +\frac{I_1-200}{5}+\frac{200-I_2}{5}-\frac{I_2}{5}\\ 
 0&=2I_1+I_1-200+200-I_2-I_2 \\ 
 0&=3I_1-2I_2\\
I_1&=\frac{2}{3}I_2\;\;\;...(i)\\
\text{also, }& I_1 +I_2-400=100\\
\text{or, }&I_1+I_2=500 \;\;\;...(ii)\\
&\text{Solvinf eq. (i) and (ii), we have}\\
I_1&=200A \text{ and }I_2=300A\\
&\text{Contribution of }S_1 \text{in 100 A at location}\\
P&=I_1-200=0A \\
&\text{Contribution of }S_2 \text{in 100 A at location}\\
P&=I_2-200=300-200=100A
\end{aligned}[/latex] Therefore, [latex]S_2[/latex] alone supplies the total load at location P.

questions.question: A two bus power system shown in the figure supplies load of 1.0+j0.5 p.u. The values of [latex]V_1[/latex] in p.u. and [latex]\delta _2[/latex] respectively are

The fuel cost functions of two power plants are Plant [latex]P_1:C_1\equiv 0.05Pg^2_1+APg_1+B[/latex] Plant [latex]P_2:C_2\equiv 0.10Pg^2_2+3APg_2+2B[/latex] where, [latex]Pg_1 \; and \; Pg_2[/latex] are the generated powers of two plants, and A and B are the
constants. If the two plants optimally share 1000 MW load at incremental fuel
cost of 100 Rs/MWh, the ratio of load shared by plants [latex]P_1 \; and \; P_2[/latex] is

questions.question:
For the given system, it is desired that the system be stable. The minimum value
of [latex]\alpha[/latex] for this condition is ______.
questions.explanation: Given, [latex]G(s)=\frac{(s+\alpha )}{s^3+(1+\alpha )s^2+(\alpha -1)s+(1-\alpha )} [/latex] and  [latex] H(s)=1[/latex] Characteristic equation of given control system is given by [latex]1+G(s)H(s)=0 [/latex] or, [latex] 1+\left [ \frac{s+\alpha }{s^3+(1+\alpha )s^2+(\alpha -1)s+(1-\alpha )} \right ]=0[/latex] or, [latex] s^3+(1+\alpha )s^2+(\alpha -1)s+(1-\alpha )+s+\alpha =0 [/latex] or,  [latex] s^3+(1+\alpha )s^2+\alpha s+1=0[/latex] Routh's array is For the given system to be stable, there should not be any sign change in the first column of Routh's array. or, [latex] 1+\left [ \frac{s+\alpha }{s^3+(1+\alpha )s^2+(\alpha -1)s+(1-\alpha )} \right ]=0[/latex]

questions.question:
The dc current flowing in a circuit is measured by two ammeters, one PMMC
and another electrodynamometer type, connected in series. The PMMC meter
contains 100 turns in the coil, the flux density in the air gap is 0.2Wb/[latex]m^2[/latex], and
the area of the coil is 80 [latex]mm^2[/latex]. The electrodynamometer ammeter has a change in
mutual inductance with respect to deflection of 0.5 mH/deg. The spring constants
of both the meters are equal. The value of current, at which the deflections of the
two meters are same, is ______
questions.explanation: For a PMMC ammeter, at equilibrim, we have : controlling torque ([latex]T_c[/latex])=Deflecting torque([latex]T_d[/latex]) [latex]\begin{aligned} K\theta _1 &=GI \; \text{or}\; \theta _1=\frac{GI}{K}\\ where, \;\; G &= nBA\\ \therefore \; \theta _1 &= \frac{nBAI}{K} \end{aligned}[/latex] For an electrodynometer ammeter, at equilibrium, Controlling torque=Deflecting torque [latex]\begin{aligned} i.e. \;\; T_c &=T_d \; \text{or}\; K \theta _2=I^2 \frac{dM}{d\theta }\\ or, \;\; \theta _2 &= \frac{I^2}{K}\cdot \frac{dM}{d\theta }\;\;...(ii)\\ \end{aligned}[/latex] For the deflection in the two meter to be same, [latex]\begin{aligned} \theta _1 &=\theta _2\\ or, \;\; \frac{nBAI}{K} &= \frac{I^2}{K}\cdot \frac{dM}{d\theta }\\ or, \;\; nBA&=I\frac{dM}{d\theta }\\ or, \;\; I &=\frac{nBA}{\left ( \frac{dM}{d\theta } \right )} \end{aligned}[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} Given, \;\; n&= \text{number of turns}=100\\ B&= 0.2 Wb/m^2\\ A&=80mm^2=80 \times 10^{-6}m^2\\ \text{and}\;\; \frac{dM}{d\theta }&=0.5 mH/rad\\ &=0.5 \times 10^{-3}H/rad \\ \end{aligned}[/latex] Putting the values in I, we get [latex]\begin{aligned} I &=\left ( \frac{100 \times 0.2 \times 80 \times 10^{-6}}{0.5 \times 10^{-3}} \right ) A\\ &= \frac{1.6}{0.5}=3.2A \end{aligned} [/latex] [latex]\therefore[/latex]  Required value of current, [latex]I=3.2Amp.[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
For a PMMC ammeter, at equilibrim, we have :
controlling torque ([latex]T_c[/latex])=Deflecting torque([latex]T_d[/latex])
[latex]\begin{aligned} K\theta _1 &=GI \; \text{or}\; \theta _1=\frac{GI}{K}\\ where, \;\; G &= nBA\\ \therefore \; \theta _1 &= \frac{nBAI}{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]
For an electrodynometer ammeter, at equilibrium,
Controlling torque=Deflecting torque
[latex]\begin{aligned} i.e. \;\; T_c &=T_d \; \text{or}\; K \theta _2=I^2 \frac{dM}{d\theta }\\ or, \;\; \theta _2 &= \frac{I^2}{K}\cdot \frac{dM}{d\theta }\;\;...(ii)\\ \end{aligned}[/latex]

For the deflection in the two meter to be same,
[latex]\begin{aligned} \theta _1 &=\theta _2\\ or, \;\; \frac{nBAI}{K} &= \frac{I^2}{K}\cdot \frac{dM}{d\theta }\\ or, \;\; nBA&=I\frac{dM}{d\theta }\\ or, \;\; I &=\frac{nBA}{\left ( \frac{dM}{d\theta } \right )} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} Given, \;\; n&= \text{number of turns}=100\\ B&= 0.2 Wb/m^2\\ A&=80mm^2=80 \times 10^{-6}m^2\\ \text{and}\;\; \frac{dM}{d\theta }&=0.5 mH/rad\\ &=0.5 \times 10^{-3}H/rad \\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
Putting the values in I, we get
[latex]\begin{aligned} I &=\left ( \frac{100 \times 0.2 \times 80 \times 10^{-6}}{0.5 \times 10^{-3}} \right ) A\\ &= \frac{1.6}{0.5}=3.2A \end{aligned} [/latex]
[latex]\therefore[/latex] Required value of current,
[latex]I=3.2Amp.[/latex]

questions.question: Consider the differential equation [latex]x^{2}\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}+x\frac{dy}{dx}-y=0[/latex]. Which of the following is a solution to this differential equation for [latex]x \gt 0[/latex] ?
questions.explanation:
[latex]\begin{aligned}
x^2\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}+x\frac{dy}{dx}-y&=0\\
\text{Let,  }x=e^z\leftrightarrow z&=\log x\\
s\frac{d}{dx}=xD=\theta &=\frac{d}{dz}\\
x^2D^2&=\theta (\theta -1)\\
(x^2D^2+xD-1)y&=0\\
[\theta (\theta -1)+\theta -1]y&=0\\
(\theta ^2-\theta +\theta -1)&=0\\
(\theta ^2-1)y&=0\\
\text{Auxiliary equation is }m^2-1&=0\\
m&=\pm 1\\
\text{CF is  }C_1e^{-z}+C_2e^z&\\
\text{Solution is   }y&=C_1e^{-z}+C_2e^z\\
y&=C_1x^{-1}+C_2x\\
y&=C_1\frac{1}{x}+C_2x
\end{aligned}[/latex] One independent solution is [latex]\frac{1}{x}[/latex] Another independent solution is x.

questions.explanation: Let, A = Area of plates Let [latex]C_1= C_3[/latex] be the capacitance formed with dielectric having dielectric constant [latex]\varepsilon _1[/latex]. Then,  [latex]C_1=C_3=\frac{\varepsilon _0\varepsilon _1A}{\frac{d}{4}}=\frac{4\varepsilon _0\varepsilon _1A}{d}[/latex] and [latex]C_2=\frac{\varepsilon _0\varepsilon _2A}{\frac{d}{2}}=\frac{2\varepsilon _0\varepsilon _2A}{d}[/latex] Also, equivalent capacitance [latex]= C_{eqv}[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} \therefore \;\;\frac{1}{C_{eqv}}&=\frac{1}{C_1}+\frac{1}{C_2}+\frac{1}{C_3}=\frac{2}{C_1}+\frac{1}{C_2} \\ &(\because \;\;C_1=C_3)(C_1,C_2,C_3 \;\text{all in series}) \\ \frac{1}{C_{eqv}} &= \frac{2d}{4\varepsilon _0\varepsilon _1d}+\frac{d}{2\varepsilon _0\varepsilon _2d}\\ C_{eqv}&=\frac{2\varepsilon _1\varepsilon _2\varepsilon _0A}{d(\varepsilon _1+\varepsilon _2)} \end{aligned}[/latex] Given, [latex]V_{eqv}=[/latex] Total Voltage = 10 VOlt, [latex]V_1=V_3=2 [/latex] Volt We know that : [latex]C\propto \frac{1}{V}[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} &\therefore \; \frac{C_{eqv}}{C_1}=\frac{V_1}{V_{eqv}}=\frac{1}{5} \\ &\frac{2\varepsilon _0\varepsilon _1\varepsilon _2 A}{d(\varepsilon _1+\varepsilon _2)}\times \frac{d}{4\varepsilon _0\varepsilon _1A}=\frac{1}{5} \\ &\frac{\varepsilon _2}{2(\varepsilon _1+\varepsilon _2)}=\frac{1}{5} \\ &5\varepsilon _2=2\varepsilon _1+2\varepsilon _2 \\ &2\varepsilon _1 =3\varepsilon _2\\ &\varepsilon _1:\varepsilon _2=3:2 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: Consider an LTI system with transfer function [latex]H(s)=\frac{1}{s(s+4)}[/latex] If the input to the system is cos(3t) and the steady state output is Asin(3t+[latex]\alpha[/latex]) , then the value of A is
questions.explanation:
Given, [latex]\begin{aligned}
H(s)&=\frac{1}{s(s+4)}\\
r(t)&=\text{input}= \cos (3t)=\cos \omega t\\
\therefore \; \omega &=3 \text{ rad/s}\\
H(j\omega)&=\frac{1}{(j\omega)(j\omega+4)}\\
\text{Now, }|H(j\omega)|&=\frac{1}{\omega \sqrt{\omega^4+4^2}}\\
&=\frac{1}{3\sqrt{25}}=\frac{1}{15} \;\;\;(at\; \omega=3)\\
\angle H(j\omega)&=-90^{\circ}-\tan ^{-1}\frac{\omega}{4}\\
&=-90^{\circ}-\tan ^{-1}\frac{3}{4}=-126.86^{\circ}\\
\therefore \; c(t)&=\frac{1}{15} \cos (3t-126.86^{\circ})\\
&=\frac{1}{15} \sin (3t-36.86^{\circ})\;\;...(i)\\
c(t)&=A \sin (3t+\alpha )\;\;...(ii)\\
\text{Comparing }&\text{ eq. (i) and (ii), we have,}\\
A&=\frac{1}{15}
\end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: Consider an LTI system with impulse response [latex]h(t)=e^{-5t}u(t)[/latex]. If the output of the system is [latex]y(t)=e^{-3t}u(t)-e^{-5t}u(t)[/latex] then the input, x(t), is given by
questions.explanation: Impulse response of an LTI system = transfer function [latex]=\frac{Y(s)}{X(s)}=H(s)[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{where, } y(t)&=e^{-3t}u(t)-e^{-5t}u(t) \\ \therefore \; Y(s) &=\frac{1}{(s+3)}-\frac{1}{(s+5)} \\ &=\frac{2}{(s+3)(s+5)} \\ \text{Also, } h(t)&=e^{-5t}u(t) \\ \therefore \; H(s) &=\frac{1}{(s+5)} \\ \text{Therefore, } X(s)&=\frac{Y(s)}{H(s)} \\ &=\frac{2}{(s+3)(s+5)} \times (s+5) \\ &= \frac{2}{(s+3)}\\ \therefore \; \text{Input}&=x(t)=2e^{-3t}u(t) \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Impulse response of an LTI system = transfer function [latex]=\frac{Y(s)}{X(s)}=H(s)[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{where, } y(t)&=e^{-3t}u(t)-e^{-5t}u(t) \\ \therefore \; Y(s) &=\frac{1}{(s+3)}-\frac{1}{(s+5)} \\ &=\frac{2}{(s+3)(s+5)} \\ \text{Also, } h(t)&=e^{-5t}u(t) \\ \therefore \; H(s) &=\frac{1}{(s+5)} \\ \text{Therefore, } X(s)&=\frac{Y(s)}{H(s)} \\ &=\frac{2}{(s+3)(s+5)} \times (s+5) \\ &= \frac{2}{(s+3)}\\ \therefore \; \text{Input}&=x(t)=2e^{-3t}u(t) \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.explanation: Closed loop transfer function, [latex]T(s)=\frac{4}{(s^2+0.4s+4)} [/latex] or, [latex]\frac{G(s)}{1+G(s)}[/latex] [latex]=\left ( \frac{4}{s^2+0.4s+4} \right )\;\;\;\;[H(s)=1] [/latex] or,  [latex](s^2+0.4s+4)=4+4G(s) [/latex] or,   [latex]G(s)=\frac{4}{s(s+0.4)} [/latex] =Open llop transfer function ( for unity feedback system) Given, input =u(t)=r(t) [latex]\therefore \;\;\; R(s)=1/s [/latex] Steady state error [latex]e_{ss}=\lim_{s \to 0}\left [ \frac{sR(s)}{1+G(s)H(s)} \right ] [/latex] [latex]\;\;=\lim_{s \to 0}\left [ \frac{sR(s)}{1+G(s)} \right ]\;\;\; [For H(s)=1] [/latex] [latex]\;\;=\lim_{s \to 0}\left [ \frac{s \times \frac{1}{s}}{1+\frac{4}{s(s+0.4)}} \right ][/latex] [latex] \;\;=\lim_{s \to 0}\left [ \frac{s(s+0.4)}{s^2+0.4s+4} \right ]=0 [/latex] [latex]\therefore[/latex]  Steady state error for step input, [latex]e_{ss}=0[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Closed loop transfer function,
[latex]T(s)=\frac{4}{(s^2+0.4s+4)} [/latex]
or, [latex]\frac{G(s)}{1+G(s)}[/latex]
[latex]=\left ( \frac{4}{s^2+0.4s+4} \right )\;\;\;\;[H(s)=1] [/latex]
or, [latex](s^2+0.4s+4)=4+4G(s) [/latex]
or, [latex]G(s)=\frac{4}{s(s+0.4)} [/latex]
=Open llop transfer function ( for unity feedback system)
Given, input =u(t)=r(t)
[latex]\therefore \;\;\; R(s)=1/s [/latex]
Steady state error
[latex]e_{ss}=\lim_{s \to 0}\left [ \frac{sR(s)}{1+G(s)H(s)} \right ] [/latex]
[latex]\;\;=\lim_{s \to 0}\left [ \frac{sR(s)}{1+G(s)} \right ]\;\;\; [For H(s)=1] [/latex]
[latex]\;\;=\lim_{s \to 0}\left [ \frac{s \times \frac{1}{s}}{1+\frac{4}{s(s+0.4)}} \right ][/latex]
[latex] \;\;=\lim_{s \to 0}\left [ \frac{s(s+0.4)}{s^2+0.4s+4} \right ]=0 [/latex]
[latex]\therefore[/latex] Steady state error for step input, [latex]e_{ss}=0[/latex]

questions.question: The state transition matrix for the system [latex]\begin{bmatrix} \dot{x_{1}}\\ \dot{x_{2}} \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 1&1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_{1}\\ x_{2} \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}u[/latex] is
questions.explanation: Given: [latex]\begin{bmatrix} \dot{x}_1\\ \dot{x}_2 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 1&1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}u [/latex] or, [latex]\;\; \dot{x}(t)=Ax(t)+Bu [/latex] Here, [latex] [A]=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 1&1 \end{bmatrix}, \;\;  B=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] State transition matric is given by, [latex]e^{At}=L^{-1}[sI-A]^{-1}[/latex] Now, [latex]  [sI-A]=\begin{bmatrix} s-1 & \\ 0 -1 & s-1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]Adj[sI-A]=\begin{bmatrix} s-1 & \\ 1 & s-1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] and [latex] |sI-A|=(s-1)^2 [/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\; [sI-A]^{-1}=\frac{1}{|sI-A|}Adj[sI-A] [/latex] [latex][sI-A]^{-1}=\frac{1}{(s-1)^2}\begin{bmatrix} s-1 & \\ 1 & s-1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s-1} & \\ \frac{1}{(s-1)^2} & \frac{1}{s-1} \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\; L^{-1}[sI-A]^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix} e^t & 0\\ te^t& e^t \end{bmatrix}[/latex] [latex] \therefore[/latex]  State transition matrix[latex]=\begin{bmatrix} e^t & 0\\ te^t& e^t \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Given: [latex]\begin{bmatrix} \dot{x}_1\\ \dot{x}_2 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 1&1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}u [/latex]
or, [latex]\;\; \dot{x}(t)=Ax(t)+Bu [/latex]
Here, [latex] [A]=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 1&1 \end{bmatrix}, \;\; B=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
State transition matric is given by,
[latex]e^{At}=L^{-1}[sI-A]^{-1}[/latex]
Now, [latex] [sI-A]=\begin{bmatrix} s-1 & \\ 0 -1 & s-1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]Adj[sI-A]=\begin{bmatrix} s-1 & \\ 1 & s-1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
and [latex] |sI-A|=(s-1)^2 [/latex]
[latex]\therefore \;\; [sI-A]^{-1}=\frac{1}{|sI-A|}Adj[sI-A] [/latex]
[latex][sI-A]^{-1}=\frac{1}{(s-1)^2}\begin{bmatrix} s-1 & \\ 1 & s-1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s-1} & \\ \frac{1}{(s-1)^2} & \frac{1}{s-1} \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]\therefore \;\; L^{-1}[sI-A]^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix} e^t & 0\\ te^t& e^t \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
[latex] \therefore[/latex] State transition matrix[latex]=\begin{bmatrix} e^t & 0\\ te^t& e^t \end{bmatrix}[/latex]

questions.question:
The saw-tooth voltage waveform shown in the figure is fed to a moving iron
voltmeter. Its reading would be close to __________
questions.explanation: Moving iron voltmeter reads rms value of voltage and current. From the given waveform of voltage, [latex]\begin{aligned} V(t) &= \left\{\begin{matrix} 50000t, & 0 \lt t \lt 0.02s\\ 50000(t-0.02). & 0.02 \lt t \lt 0.04s \end{matrix}\right.\\ \therefore \; V_{rms} &= \sqrt{\frac{1}{T}\int_{0}^{T}(V(T)^2 \; dt}\\ &= \sqrt{\frac{1}{0.04} \int_{0}^{0.02} (50000t)^2 \; dt +\int_{0.02}^{0.04}(50000(t-0.02))^2 \; dt}\\ &= 25000\sqrt{\left [ \frac{t^3}{3} \right ]_0^{0.02}+\left [ \frac{(t-0.02)^3}{3} \right ]_{0.02}^{0.04}}\\ &= 25000\sqrt{\frac{1}{3}\left [ (0.02)^3+(0.02)^3 \right ]}\\ &= 57.73 \text{Volt} \end{aligned} [/latex] [latex]\therefore [/latex]  Voltage reading by moving iron voltmeter =57.73 Volts

questions.question: While measuring power of a three-phase balanced load by the two-wattmeter method, the readings are 100 W and 250 W. The power factor of the load is ______.
questions.explanation: Given, [latex]W_1=250W[/latex], [latex]W_2=100W[/latex] Power factor angle is given by [latex]\begin{aligned} \phi &= \tan^{-1}\left [ \frac{\sqrt{3}(W_1-W_2)}{W_1+W_2} \right ]\\ &=\tan^{-1}\left [ \frac{\sqrt{3}(250-100)}{250+100} \right ] \\ &= \tan^{-1}\left [ \frac{\sqrt{3}\times 150}{350} \right ]\\ &= \tan^{-1}\left [ \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{7} \right ]=36.58^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex] Therefore, power factor of load [latex]= \cos \phi =\cos 36.58^{\circ} =0.802=0.80[/latex]

questions.question: A step-up chopper is used to feed a load at 400 V dc from a 250 V dc source. The inductor current is continuous. If the 'off' time of the switch is 20 [latex]\mu[/latex]s, the switching frequency of the chopper in kHz is _____.
questions.explanation: Given step up chopper, [latex]\begin{aligned} V_0&=400V\\ V_s&=250V\\ T_{OFF}&=2 \times 10^{-6} sec\\ V_0&=V_s \times \frac{T}{T_{OFF}}\\ 400&=250 \times \frac{T}{20 \times 10^{-6}}\\ T&=\frac{400 \times 20 \times 10^{-6}}{250}\\ &=3.2 \times 10^{-5}\; sec\\ f&=\frac{1}{T}=\frac{1}{3.2 \times 10^{-5}}\\ f&=31.2jHz \end{aligned}[/latex]

Given step up chopper,

questions.explanation: [latex]\int_{0}^{8}\left ( \int_{y/2}^{(y/2)+1} \left ( \frac{2x-y}{2} \right )dx\right ) dy[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{2x-y}{2} &=u \\ x-\frac{y}{2}&=u \\ dx&= du\\ \text{at }x &=\frac{y}{2} \\ u&=\frac{\frac{2y}{2}-y}{2}=0 \\ \text{at }x &=\frac{y}{2}+1 \\ u &=\frac{2\left ( \frac{y}{2}+1 \right )-y}{2}\\ &=\frac{y+2-y}{2}=1 \end{aligned}[/latex] Thus, integral becomes [latex]\int_{0}^{8}\left (\int_{0}^{1} u du \right )dy[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} v&=\frac{y}{2} \\ dv&=\frac{dy}{2} \\ y=0&= \\ \Rightarrow \;\; v &= 0\\ &y=8 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; v &= 4\\ &\;\;=\int_{0}^{4}\left ( \int_{0}^{1} udu\right )\times 2dv\\ &\;\;= \int_{0}^{4}\left ( \int_{0}^{1} 2udu\right )\times dv \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\int_{0}^{8}\left ( \int_{y/2}^{(y/2)+1} \left ( \frac{2x-y}{2} \right )dx\right ) dy[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{2x-y}{2} &=u \\ x-\frac{y}{2}&=u \\ dx&= du\\ \text{at }x &=\frac{y}{2} \\ u&=\frac{\frac{2y}{2}-y}{2}=0 \\ \text{at }x &=\frac{y}{2}+1 \\ u &=\frac{2\left ( \frac{y}{2}+1 \right )-y}{2}\\ &=\frac{y+2-y}{2}=1 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Thus, integral becomes [latex]\int_{0}^{8}\left (\int_{0}^{1} u du \right )dy[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} v&=\frac{y}{2} \\ dv&=\frac{dy}{2} \\ y=0&= \\ \Rightarrow \;\; v &= 0\\ &y=8 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; v &= 4\\ &\;\;=\int_{0}^{4}\left ( \int_{0}^{1} udu\right )\times 2dv\\ &\;\;= \int_{0}^{4}\left ( \int_{0}^{1} 2udu\right )\times dv \end{aligned}[/latex]

The minimum value of the function [latex]f(x)=x^{3}-3x^{2}-24x+100[/latex] in the interval
[-3, 3] is
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} f(x)&=x^3-3x^2-24x+100\;\;\;x \in [-3,3]\\ f'(x)&=3x^2-6x-24\\ f'(x)&=0 \; at \; x=4,-2 \end{aligned}[/latex] Critical points are [-3,-2,3] [latex]\begin{aligned} f(-3)&=-27-27+72+100=118\\ f(-2)&=-8-12+48+100=128\\ f(3)&=27-27-72+100=28 \end{aligned}[/latex] Hence f(x) has minimum value at x=3 which is 28.
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{aligned} f(x)&=x^3-3x^2-24x+100\;\;\;x \in [-3,3]\\ f'(x)&=3x^2-6x-24\\ f'(x)&=0 \; at \; x=4,-2 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Critical points are [-3,-2,3]

questions.explanation: Given that, [latex]\begin{bmatrix} X_1(K+1)\\X_2(K+1) \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} a & a-1\\ a+1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} X_1(K)\\X_2(K) \end{bmatrix}[/latex] With initial conditions, [latex]X_1(0)=1,\;\;X_2(0)=0[/latex] For a=1, we can write, [latex]\begin{bmatrix} X_1(K+1)\\X_2(K+1) \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} X_1(K)\\X_2(K+) \end{bmatrix}[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \; X_1(K+1)=X_1(K) \;\;...(i)[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \; X_2(K+1)=2X_1(K)+X_2(k) \;\;...(ii)[/latex] Applying z-transform on equation (i), [latex]\begin{aligned} zX_1(z)-zX_1(0)&=X_1(z) \\ X_1(z)[z-1]&=zX_1(0) \\ X_1(z) =\frac{z}{z-1}\;\;&[Given, \; X_1(0)=1]...(iii) \\ \text{from equation (ii),}\\ zX_2(z)-zX_2(0)&=2X_1(z)+X_2(z)\\ X_2(z)[z-1]&=2X_1(z)+zX_2(0)\\ [Given,\;\; X_2(0)&=0]\\ \frac{X_2(z)}{X_1(z)}&=\frac{2}{z-1} \end{aligned}[/latex] Thus, transfer function, [latex]H(z)=\frac{2}{z-1}[/latex] Therefore, pole location is z=1.

questions.question:
An input signal x(t)=2+5sin(100[latex]\pi[/latex]t) is sampled with a sampling frequency of
400 Hz and applied to the system whose transfer function is represented by [latex]\frac{Y(z)}{X(z)}=\frac{1}{N}(\frac{1-z^{-N}}{1-z^{-1}})[/latex] where, N represents the number of samples per cycle. The output y(n) of the system under steady state is
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} f_s&= 400Hz\\ x(t)&=2+5 \sin (100 \pi t) \\ t\rightarrow xT_s &=\frac{n}{f_s}=\frac{n}{400} \\ x(n)&=2+5 \sin \left ( 100 \pi\frac{n}{400} \right ) \\ &= 2+5 \sin \frac{\pi}{4}n\\ \text{Here, }\omega _0 &=\frac{\pi}{4} \end{aligned}[/latex] Therefore, N= time-period of [latex]x(n)=\frac{2 \pi }{\omega _0}=\frac{2 \pi}{\pi/4}=0[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Now, }H(z)&=\frac{1}{N}\left [ \frac{1-z^{-N}}{1-z^{-1}} \right ] \\ \text{Applying, }z &=e^{j\omega } \\ H(e^{j\omega }) &= \frac{1}{N}\left [ \frac{1-e^{-j\omega N}}{1-e^{-j\omega }} \right ] \\ \text{For, } &\text{sinusoidal part of }x(n): \\ H(e^{j\omega _0 }) &= \frac{1}{N}\left [ \frac{1-e^{-j\omega _0 N}}{1-e^{-j\omega _0 }} \right ] \\ [\text{Note: }] \omega _0 N&=\frac{\pi}{4} \times 8 =2 \pi] \\ &= \frac{1}{N}\left [ \frac{1-e^{-j2 \pi N}}{1-e^{-j \pi/4}} \right ]=0 \end{aligned}[/latex] Therefore, for sinusoidal part of input, system output is zero. For dc part of input, [latex]\begin{aligned} y(n)&=\text{output}\\ &=H(e^{j0}) \times \text{input dc value}\\ [\because \; &H(e^{j\omega })_{\omega =0}=1]\\ &=1 \times 2=2 \end{aligned}[/latex] Thus, steady state output = 2
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{aligned} f_s&= 400Hz\\ x(t)&=2+5 \sin (100 \pi t) \\ t\rightarrow xT_s &=\frac{n}{f_s}=\frac{n}{400} \\ x(n)&=2+5 \sin \left ( 100 \pi\frac{n}{400} \right ) \\ &= 2+5 \sin \frac{\pi}{4}n\\ \text{Here, }\omega _0 &=\frac{\pi}{4} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Therefore, N= time-period of [latex]x(n)=\frac{2 \pi }{\omega _0}=\frac{2 \pi}{\pi/4}=0[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Now, }H(z)&=\frac{1}{N}\left [ \frac{1-z^{-N}}{1-z^{-1}} \right ] \\ \text{Applying, }z &=e^{j\omega } \\ H(e^{j\omega }) &= \frac{1}{N}\left [ \frac{1-e^{-j\omega N}}{1-e^{-j\omega }} \right ] \\ \text{For, } &\text{sinusoidal part of }x(n): \\ H(e^{j\omega _0 }) &= \frac{1}{N}\left [ \frac{1-e^{-j\omega _0 N}}{1-e^{-j\omega _0 }} \right ] \\ [\text{Note: }] \omega _0 N&=\frac{\pi}{4} \times 8 =2 \pi] \\ &= \frac{1}{N}\left [ \frac{1-e^{-j2 \pi N}}{1-e^{-j \pi/4}} \right ]=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Therefore, for sinusoidal part of input, system output is zero. For dc part of input,
[latex]\begin{aligned} y(n)&=\text{output}\\ &=H(e^{j0}) \times \text{input dc value}\\ [\because \; &H(e^{j\omega })_{\omega =0}=1]\\ &=1 \times 2=2 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Thus, steady state output = 2

questions.question: A 250 V dc shunt machine has armature circuit resistance of 0.6 [latex]\Omega[/latex] and field circuit resistance of 125 [latex]\Omega[/latex]. The machine is connected to 250 V supply mains. The motor is operated as a generator and then as a motor separately. The line current of the machine in both the cases is 50 A. The ratio of the speed as a generator to the speed as a motor is _____.
questions.explanation: Given, [latex]V=250V, [/latex]  [latex]R_a=0.6\Omega , [/latex]  [latex]R_f=125\Omega , [/latex]  [latex]I_L=50A[/latex]  both for motor as well as generator action. Field current, [latex]I_f=\frac{V}{R_f}=\frac{250}{125}=2A [/latex] [latex]\text{For motor action:} [/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} E_{a_m}&= V-I_aR_a\\ I_a&=I_l-I_f=50-2=48A \\ \therefore \; E_{a_m}&=250-48 \times 0.6 \\ &=221.2 V \\ \end{aligned} [/latex] [latex]\text{For generator action:} [/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} E_{a_g} &=V+I_aR_a \\ I_a &= I_L+I_f=50+2=52A\\ \therefore \; E_{a_g} &=250+52 \times 0.6=281.2V \end{aligned} [/latex] For a DC shunt machine, [latex]E_a\propto \phi \omega _n [/latex] or   [latex] \;\; E_a\propto N  \;\text{(speed)}[/latex]    [latex] (\because \;\phi =constant)[/latex] [latex] \therefore \;\;\frac{E_{a_g}}{E_{a_m}}=\frac{N_g}{N_m} [/latex] [latex]\frac{N_g}{N_m}=\frac{281.2}{221.2}=1.271 [/latex] Therefore, ratio of the speed as a generator to the speed of motor=1.271
questions.explanation_html:
Given, [latex]V=250V, [/latex] [latex]R_a=0.6\Omega , [/latex] [latex]R_f=125\Omega , [/latex] [latex]I_L=50A[/latex] both for motor as well as generator action.
Field current,
[latex]I_f=\frac{V}{R_f}=\frac{250}{125}=2A [/latex]
[latex]\text{For motor action:} [/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} E_{a_m}&= V-I_aR_a\\ I_a&=I_l-I_f=50-2=48A \\ \therefore \; E_{a_m}&=250-48 \times 0.6 \\ &=221.2 V \\ \end{aligned} [/latex]
[latex]\text{For generator action:} [/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} E_{a_g} &=V+I_aR_a \\ I_a &= I_L+I_f=50+2=52A\\ \therefore \; E_{a_g} &=250+52 \times 0.6=281.2V \end{aligned} [/latex]
For a DC shunt machine, [latex]E_a\propto \phi \omega _n [/latex]
or [latex] \;\; E_a\propto N \;\text{(speed)}[/latex] [latex] (\because \;\phi =constant)[/latex]
[latex] \therefore \;\;\frac{E_{a_g}}{E_{a_m}}=\frac{N_g}{N_m} [/latex]
[latex]\frac{N_g}{N_m}=\frac{281.2}{221.2}=1.271 [/latex]
Therefore, ratio of the speed as a generator to the speed of motor=1.271

questions.question: A 20-pole alternators is having 180 identical stator slots with 6 conductors in each slot. All the coils of a phase are in series. If the coils are connected to realize single-phase winding, the generated voltage is [latex]V_1[/latex]. If the coils are reconnected to realize three phase star connected winding, the generated phase voltage is [latex]V_2[/latex]. Assuming full pitch, single-layer winding, the ratio [latex]V_1/V_2[/latex] is
For a single phase, two winding transformer, the supply frequency and voltage are both increased by 10%. The percentage changes in the hysteresis loss and eddy current loss, respectively, are
questions.explanation: Eddy current loss, [latex]P_a\propto B_m^2 f^2[/latex] and Hysteresis loss, [latex]\begin{aligned} P_h &\propto B_m^x f\propto B_m^{1.6}f \\ \text{when}\;\; \frac{V}{f} &= \text{constant}, \\ P_e&\propto V^2 \\ \text{and}\;\; P_h &\propto \frac{V^{1.6}}{f^{0.6}} \\ \text{Given} \;\; V_2&=1.1V_1 \\ \text{and}\;\; f_2&= 1.1f_1 \\ \frac{P_{e_2}}{P_{e_1}}=\left ( \frac{V_2}{V_1} \right )^2\\ &=(1.1)^2=1.21\\ \frac{P_{e_2}-P_{e_1}}{P_{e_1}}&=0.21 \end{aligned} [/latex] Therefore, % increase in eddy current loss [latex]\begin{aligned} &= \left [ \frac{P_{e_2}-P_{e_1}}{P_{e_1}}\right ] \times 100\%=21\%\\ \text{also}\;\; \frac{P_{h_2}}{P_{h_1}}&= \left ( \frac{V_2}{V_1} \right )^{1.6} \times \left ( \frac{f_1}{f_2} \right )^{0.6}\\ &=(1.1)^{1.6} \times \left ( \frac{1}{1.1} \right )^{0.6}=1.1\\ \text{or}\;\; \frac{P_{h_2}-P_{h_1}}{P_{h_1}}&= 0.1 \end{aligned}[/latex] Therefore, % increase in hysteresis loss [latex]=\left ( \frac{P_{h_2}-P_{h_1}}{P_{h_1}} \right ) \times 100\%=10\%[/latex] Thus, hysteresis loss increased by 10% and eddy current loss by 21%.

Therefore, % increase in eddy current loss
[latex]\begin{aligned} &= \left [ \frac{P_{e_2}-P_{e_1}}{P_{e_1}}\right ] \times 100\%=21\%\\ \text{also}\;\; \frac{P_{h_2}}{P_{h_1}}&= \left ( \frac{V_2}{V_1} \right )^{1.6} \times \left ( \frac{f_1}{f_2} \right )^{0.6}\\ &=(1.1)^{1.6} \times \left ( \frac{1}{1.1} \right )^{0.6}=1.1\\ \text{or}\;\; \frac{P_{h_2}-P_{h_1}}{P_{h_1}}&= 0.1 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A synchronous generator is connected to an infinite bus with excitation voltage [latex]E_f= 1.3[/latex] pu. The generator has a synchronous reactance of 1.1 pu and is delivering real power (P) of 0.6 pu to the bus. Assume the infinite bus voltage to be 1.0 pu. Neglect stator resistance. The reactive power (Q) in pu supplied by the generator to the bus under this condition is _____.
questions.explanation: Given, [latex]E_f=1.3pu, X_s=1.1pu, V=1 pu, P=0.6pu[/latex] Neglecting stator resistance i.e. [latex]\theta _s=90^{\circ}[/latex] Output power delivered, [latex]\begin{aligned} P &=\frac{VE_f}{X_s}\sin \delta \\ \sin \delta &=\frac{PX_s}{VE_f} \\ &= \frac{0.6 \times 1.1}{1 \times 1.3}\approx 0.5\\ \therefore \;\; \delta &=30^{\circ}=\text{Power angle} \\ \therefore \;\; \cos \delta &= \cos 30^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \end{aligned}[/latex] Reactive power is given by, [latex]\begin{aligned} Q&=\left [ \frac{VE_f}{X_s} \cos \delta -\frac{V^2}{X_s} \right ]\\ &=\left [ \frac{1 \times 1.3}{1.1} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{1^2}{1.1} \right ]\\ Q&=(1.023-0.909)=0.114pu\\ &\approx 0.11pu \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:

Output power delivered,
[latex]\begin{aligned} P &=\frac{VE_f}{X_s}\sin \delta \\ \sin \delta &=\frac{PX_s}{VE_f} \\ &= \frac{0.6 \times 1.1}{1 \times 1.3}\approx 0.5\\ \therefore \;\; \delta &=30^{\circ}=\text{Power angle} \\ \therefore \;\; \cos \delta &= \cos 30^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Reactive power is given by,
[latex]\begin{aligned} Q&=\left [ \frac{VE_f}{X_s} \cos \delta -\frac{V^2}{X_s} \right ]\\ &=\left [ \frac{1 \times 1.3}{1.1} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{1^2}{1.1} \right ]\\ Q&=(1.023-0.909)=0.114pu\\ &\approx 0.11pu \end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Now, }\frac{51.5-f}{P_1}&=1=droop \\ P_1&= (51.5-f)\;\;...(i)\\ \text{Also, } \left ( \frac{51-f}{2.5-P_1} \right )&=1=droop \\ 51-f &=2.5-P_1 \\ P_1 &=f-48.5 \;\;...(ii) \\ \text{equating eq. }&\text{(i) and (ii), we get,} \\ 51.5-f &=f-48.5 \\ 2f&=100 \\ f&=50Hz \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A three phase, 100 MVA, 25 kV generator has solidly grounded neutral. The positive, negative, and the zero sequence reactances of the generator are 0.2 pu, 0.2 pu and 0.05 pu, respectively, at the machine base quantities. If a bolted single phase to ground fault occurs at the terminal of the unloaded generator, the fault current in amperes immediately after the fault is_____.
questions.explanation: Given, [latex]X_1=0.2pu, X_2=0.2pu, X_3=0.05pu[/latex] For a line-to-ground fault on generator, fault current is given by [latex]\begin{aligned} I_{f_{LG}}&=3I_{R_0} =3I_{R_1}=3I_{R_2}\\ &= \frac{3E}{Z_1+Z_2+Z_3}\\ &=\frac{3 \times 1}{0.2+0.2+0.05} \\ &= \frac{3}{0.45}=\frac{20}{3}pu \end{aligned}[/latex] Also, base MVA =100 Base KVA =25 Theerefore, Base current, [latex]I_b=\frac{100 \times 10^6}{\sqrt{3} \times 25 \times 10^3}=2.309kA[/latex] Actual fault current in ampere [latex]=(I_{f_{LG}})_{pu} \times I_b=\frac{20}{30} \times 2.309 \times 10^3[/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\;I_f=15393 \text{ Ampere}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Given, [latex]X_1=0.2pu, X_2=0.2pu, X_3=0.05pu[/latex]
For a line-to-ground fault on generator, fault current is given by
[latex]\begin{aligned} I_{f_{LG}}&=3I_{R_0} =3I_{R_1}=3I_{R_2}\\ &= \frac{3E}{Z_1+Z_2+Z_3}\\ &=\frac{3 \times 1}{0.2+0.2+0.05} \\ &= \frac{3}{0.45}=\frac{20}{3}pu \end{aligned}[/latex]
Also, base MVA =100
Base KVA =25
Theerefore, Base current,
[latex]I_b=\frac{100 \times 10^6}{\sqrt{3} \times 25 \times 10^3}=2.309kA[/latex]
Actual fault current in ampere
[latex]=(I_{f_{LG}})_{pu} \times I_b=\frac{20}{30} \times 2.309 \times 10^3[/latex]
[latex]\therefore \;\;I_f=15393 \text{ Ampere}[/latex]

questions.question: A system with the open loop transfer function [latex]G(s)=\frac{K}{s(s+2)(s^{2}+2s+2)}[/latex] is connected in a negative feedback configuration with a feedback gain of unity. For the closed loop system to be marginally stable, the value of K is ______
questions.explanation: Given, [latex]G(s)=\frac{K}{s(s+2)(s^2+2s+2)}[/latex] The characteristic equation of given unity-negative feedback control system is given by [latex]1+G(s)H(s)=0[/latex] or,  [latex] 1+\frac{K}{s(s+2)(s^3+2s+2)}=0 [/latex] or,  [latex]s(s+2)(s^3+2s+2)+K=0 [/latex] or,  [latex]s^4+4s^3+6s^2+4s+K=0 [/latex] Forming Routh' array as shown below For stability of the system, [latex]K \gt 0[/latex] and [latex]\frac{20-4K}{5} \gt 0 [/latex]or [latex]K\gt 5 [/latex] [latex]\therefore[/latex]  For stability,  [latex]0 \lt K \lt 5[/latex] For given system to be marginally stable K=5
questions.explanation_html:
Given, [latex]G(s)=\frac{K}{s(s+2)(s^2+2s+2)}[/latex]

The characteristic equation of given unity-negative feedback control system is given by
[latex]1+G(s)H(s)=0[/latex]
or, [latex] 1+\frac{K}{s(s+2)(s^3+2s+2)}=0 [/latex]
or, [latex]s(s+2)(s^3+2s+2)+K=0 [/latex]
or, [latex]s^4+4s^3+6s^2+4s+K=0 [/latex]
Forming Routh' array as shown below

For stability of the system, [latex]K \gt 0[/latex] and [latex]\frac{20-4K}{5} \gt 0 [/latex]or [latex]K\gt 5 [/latex]
[latex]\therefore[/latex] For stability, [latex]0 \lt K \lt 5[/latex]
For given system to be marginally stable

K=5

questions.question: For the transfer function [latex]G(s)=\frac{5(s+4)}{s(s+0.25)(s^{2}+4s+25)}[/latex] The values of the constant gain term and the highest corner frequency of the Bode plot respectively are
questions.explanation: Given, [latex]G(s)=\frac{5(s+4)}{s(s+0.25)(s^2+4s+25)} [/latex] Reducing G(s) in time constant form, we have: [latex] G(s)=\frac{5 \times 4\left ( 1+\frac{s}{4} \right )}{s\left [ 0.25\left ( 1+\frac{s}{0.25} \right ) \right ]\left [ 25\left ( 1+\frac{4}{25}s+\frac{1}{25}s^2 \right ) \right ]} [/latex] [latex]=\frac{20(1+0.25s)}{s[0.25(1+4s)][25(1+0.16s+0.04s^2)]} [/latex] [latex]G(s)=\frac{3.2(1+0.25s)}{s(1+4s)(1+0.16s+0.04s^2)} [/latex] [latex]\therefore[/latex]  The value of constant gain term =3.2 Also,  [latex]G(j\omega )=\frac{3.2\left ( 1+\frac{j\omega }{4} \right )}{(j\omega)\left ( 1+\frac{j\omega}{0.25} \right )\left ( 1+j0.16\omega -\frac{\omega ^2}{25} \right )} [/latex] Corner frequencies are: [latex]\omega _1=4[/latex] rad/sec [latex]\omega _2=0.25[/latex] rad/sec [latex] \omega _3=5[/latex] rad/sec [latex] \therefore[/latex]  Highest corner frequency [latex]=\omega _3=5[/latex] rad/sec
questions.explanation_html:
Given, [latex]G(s)=\frac{5(s+4)}{s(s+0.25)(s^2+4s+25)} [/latex]
Reducing G(s) in time constant form, we have:
[latex] G(s)=\frac{5 \times 4\left ( 1+\frac{s}{4} \right )}{s\left [ 0.25\left ( 1+\frac{s}{0.25} \right ) \right ]\left [ 25\left ( 1+\frac{4}{25}s+\frac{1}{25}s^2 \right ) \right ]} [/latex]
[latex]=\frac{20(1+0.25s)}{s[0.25(1+4s)][25(1+0.16s+0.04s^2)]} [/latex]
[latex]G(s)=\frac{3.2(1+0.25s)}{s(1+4s)(1+0.16s+0.04s^2)} [/latex]
[latex]\therefore[/latex] The value of constant gain term =3.2
Also, [latex]G(j\omega )=\frac{3.2\left ( 1+\frac{j\omega }{4} \right )}{(j\omega)\left ( 1+\frac{j\omega}{0.25} \right )\left ( 1+j0.16\omega -\frac{\omega ^2}{25} \right )} [/latex]
Corner frequencies are:
[latex]\omega _1=4[/latex] rad/sec
[latex]\omega _2=0.25[/latex] rad/sec
[latex] \omega _3=5[/latex] rad/sec
[latex] \therefore[/latex] Highest corner frequency [latex]=\omega _3=5[/latex] rad/sec

questions.question: The second order dynamic system [latex]\frac{dX}{dt}=PX+Qu  [/latex] [latex] y=RX[/latex] has the matrices P, Q and R as follows : [latex]P=\begin{bmatrix} -1 &1 \\ 0&-3 \end{bmatrix}\; Q=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \; R=\begin{bmatrix} 0 &1 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] The system has the following controllability and observability properties:
questions.explanation: Given: [latex]\dot{x}(t)=Px+Qu [/latex] [latex]y=Rx [/latex] [latex]P=\begin{bmatrix} -1 &1 \\ 0& -3 \end{bmatrix} [/latex],  [latex]Q=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}[/latex],   [latex] R=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] For controllability, [latex] Q_c=\begin{bmatrix} Q &PQ \end{bmatrix}[/latex] [latex] [PQ]=\begin{bmatrix} -1 &1 \\ 0& -3 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -3 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\; Q_c=\begin{bmatrix} 0 &1 \\ 1& -3 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\;|Q_c|=-1\neq 0\Rightarrow \;\; controllable [/latex] Also, for observability, [latex] Q_0=\begin{bmatrix} R^T & P^TR^T \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]\begin{bmatrix} P^T & R^T \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 & 0\\ 1 & -3 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ -3 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\;Q_0=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0\\ 1 & -3 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\; |Q_0|=(0 \times -3 -0 \times 1)=0\Rightarrow \;\; non-observable[/latex] Since, [latex] Q_c\neq 0[/latex] and [latex]Q_0=0[/latex] [latex] \therefore[/latex]  System is controllable but not observable.
questions.explanation_html:
Given: [latex]\dot{x}(t)=Px+Qu [/latex]
[latex]y=Rx [/latex]
[latex]P=\begin{bmatrix} -1 &1 \\ 0& -3 \end{bmatrix} [/latex], [latex]Q=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}[/latex], [latex] R=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
For controllability,
[latex] Q_c=\begin{bmatrix} Q &PQ \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
[latex] [PQ]=\begin{bmatrix} -1 &1 \\ 0& -3 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -3 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]\therefore \;\; Q_c=\begin{bmatrix} 0 &1 \\ 1& -3 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]\therefore \;\;|Q_c|=-1\neq 0\Rightarrow \;\; controllable [/latex]
Also, for observability,
[latex] Q_0=\begin{bmatrix} R^T & P^TR^T \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]\begin{bmatrix} P^T & R^T \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 & 0\\ 1 & -3 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ -3 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]\therefore \;\;Q_0=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0\\ 1 & -3 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]\therefore \;\; |Q_0|=(0 \times -3 -0 \times 1)=0\Rightarrow \;\; non-observable[/latex]
Since, [latex] Q_c\neq 0[/latex] and [latex]Q_0=0[/latex]
[latex] \therefore[/latex] System is controllable but not observable.

questions.question:
Suppose that resistors [latex]R_1 \; and \; R_2[/latex] are connected in parallel to give an equivalent resistor R. If resistors [latex]R_1 \; and \; R_2[/latex] have tolerance of 1% each, the equivalent resistor R for resistors [latex]R_1 = 300 \Omega[/latex]
 and [latex]R_2 = 200 \Omega[/latex] will have tolerance of
questions.explanation: Given,[latex]R_1=300\Omega ,[/latex]  [latex] R_2=200\Omega [/latex] Equivalent resistance of parallel combination of [latex]R_1[/latex] and [latex]R_2[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} R &=\frac{R_1R_2}{R_1+R_2} =\frac{300 \times 200}{500}\\ &= 120\Omega =R_T\\ \text{Given tolerance of} \; R_1&=1\% \\ \therefore \; R_1 &= 300 \pm 3\\ R_1 &= 303 \Omega \; \text{or} 297\Omega \\ \text{Tolerance of} \; R_2&=1\% \\ \therefore \; R_2 &= 200 \pm 2\\ R_2 &= 202 \Omega \; \text{or} 198\Omega \end{aligned} [/latex] Equivalent resistance of the parallel combination of [latex]R_1[/latex] and [latex]R_2[/latex] in high range is: [latex] R_H=\frac{303 \times 202}{303+202}=121.2\Omega [/latex] [latex]\therefore[/latex]  Tolerance for equivalent resistance R in high range of [latex]R_1[/latex] and [latex]R_2[/latex] is [latex]\begin{aligned} \varepsilon _R &=\left ( \frac{R_H-R}{R} \right ) \times 100\% \\ &= \left ( \frac{121.2-120}{120} \right ) \times 100\% \\ &= \frac{1.2}{120} \times 100\%=1\% \end{aligned} [/latex] Note: In low range of [latex]R_1[/latex] and [latex]R_2[/latex], [latex]R_L=\left ( \frac{297 \times 198}{495} \right )=118.8\Omega [/latex] [latex]\therefore[/latex]  Tolerance of equivalent resistance, R in low range is, [latex]\begin{aligned} \varepsilon _L &=\left ( \frac{R_L-R}{R} \right ) \times 100\% \\ &= \left ( \frac{118.8-120}{120} \right ) \times 100\% \\ &= -1\% \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Given,[latex]R_1=300\Omega ,[/latex] [latex] R_2=200\Omega [/latex]
Equivalent resistance of parallel combination of [latex]R_1[/latex] and [latex]R_2[/latex]

[latex]\begin{aligned} R &=\frac{R_1R_2}{R_1+R_2} =\frac{300 \times 200}{500}\\ &= 120\Omega =R_T\\ \text{Given tolerance of} \; R_1&=1\% \\ \therefore \; R_1 &= 300 \pm 3\\ R_1 &= 303 \Omega \; \text{or} 297\Omega \\ \text{Tolerance of} \; R_2&=1\% \\ \therefore \; R_2 &= 200 \pm 2\\ R_2 &= 202 \Omega \; \text{or} 198\Omega \end{aligned} [/latex]
Equivalent resistance of the parallel combination of [latex]R_1[/latex] and [latex]R_2[/latex] in high range is:
[latex] R_H=\frac{303 \times 202}{303+202}=121.2\Omega [/latex]
[latex]\therefore[/latex] Tolerance for equivalent resistance R in high range of [latex]R_1[/latex] and [latex]R_2[/latex] is
[latex]\begin{aligned} \varepsilon _R &=\left ( \frac{R_H-R}{R} \right ) \times 100\% \\ &= \left ( \frac{121.2-120}{120} \right ) \times 100\% \\ &= \frac{1.2}{120} \times 100\%=1\% \end{aligned} [/latex]
Note: In low range of [latex]R_1[/latex] and [latex]R_2[/latex],
[latex]R_L=\left ( \frac{297 \times 198}{495} \right )=118.8\Omega [/latex]
[latex]\therefore[/latex] Tolerance of equivalent resistance, R in low range is,
[latex]\begin{aligned} \varepsilon _L &=\left ( \frac{R_L-R}{R} \right ) \times 100\% \\ &= \left ( \frac{118.8-120}{120} \right ) \times 100\% \\ &= -1\% \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question:
Two ammeters X and Y have resistances of 1.2 [latex]\Omega[/latex] and 1.5 [latex]\Omega[/latex] respectively and they give full-scale deflection with 150 mA and 250 mA respectively. The ranges have been extended by connecting shunts so as to give full scale deflection with 15 A. The ammeters along with shunts are connected in parallel and then placed
in a circuit in which the total current flowing is 15 A. The current in amperes indicated in ammeter X is_____.
questions.explanation:
Given, [latex]R_{m_X}=1.2\Omega , [/latex] [latex]R_{m_Y}=1.5\Omega[/latex] [latex] I_{m_X}=0.15A, [/latex] [latex]I_{m_Y}=0.25A [/latex] and  [latex] I= [/latex] full scale deflection current=15A [latex]\therefore[/latex] Shunt multiplying factor for ammeter X is [latex]m_X=\frac{I}{I_{m_X}}=\frac{15}{0.15}=100[/latex] and shunt multiplier resistance, [latex]R_{{sh}_X}=\frac{R_{m_X}}{(m_X-1)}=\frac{12}{99}=0.012\Omega[/latex] Also, shunt multiplying factor for ammeteer Y is [latex]m_Y=\frac{I}{I_{m_Y}}=\frac{15}{0.25}=60 [/latex] and shunt multiplier resistance, [latex]R_{{sh}_Y}=\frac{R_{m_Y}}{(m_Y-1)}=\frac{1.5}{59}=0.025\Omega[/latex] when these ammeters are connected in parrelel as shown in the figure below, Let current in ammeter X be [latex]I_X[/latex] then, [latex]\begin{aligned}
R_X&=\left ( \frac{ R_{{sh}_X} \cdot R_{m_X}} { R_{{sh}_X}+R_{m_X}} \right )\\
 &= \left ( \frac{0.012 \times 1.2}{1.212} \right )\\ 
 &= 0.011 \Omega \\ 
R_Y &=\left ( \frac{R_{{sh}_Y}\cdot R_{m_Y}}{R_{{sh}_Y}+R_{m_Y}} \right )\\ 
 &= \left ( \frac{0.025 \times 1.5}{1.525} \right )\\ 
 &=0.024\Omega  \\ 
\therefore \; I_X &=\left (\frac{R_Y}{R_X+R_Y}   \right )\times 15 \\ 
 &=\left ( \frac{0.024}{0.035} \right ) \times 15 \\ 
 &= 10.28A
\end{aligned}[/latex] [latex]
\therefore[/latex]  Current in ammeter X=10.28A

questions.question: An oscillator circuit using ideal op-amp and diodes is shown in the figure. The time duration for +ve part of the cycle is [latex]\Delta t_{1}[/latex] and for -ve part is [latex]\Delta t_{2}[/latex]. The value of [latex]e^{\frac{\Delta t_{1}-\Delta t_{2}}{RC}}[/latex] will be ______.
questions.explanation: This circuit is a stable multivibrator (or) free running oscillator. When [latex]V_0=+V_{sat} [/latex] [latex]V_{UPT}=V_{sat}\times \frac{1k\Omega }{1k\Omega +3k\Omega } = \frac{V_{sat}}{4} [/latex] When,   [latex] V_0=-V_{sat} [/latex] [latex]V_{LTP}=V_{sat}\times \frac{1k\Omega }{1k\Omega +1k\Omega }=\frac{-V_{sat}}{2}[/latex] [latex]V_c=V_{final}+(V_{inital}-V_{final})e^{-t/RC}[/latex] In time  [latex] t=\Delta t_1[/latex] [latex] V_c=V_{UTP}; [/latex] [latex]V_{initial}=V_{LTP};[/latex] [latex]V_{final}=+V_{sat}[/latex] [latex]V_{UTP}=V_{sat}+(V_{LTP}-V_{sat})e^{-\Delta t_1/RC} [/latex] [latex]\frac{V_{sat}}{4}=V_{sat}+\left ( -\frac{V_{sat}}{2}-V_{sat} \right )e^{-\Delta t_1/RC} [/latex] [latex]V_{sat}\left ( -1+\frac{1}{4} \right )=-V_{sat}\left ( \frac{1}{2}+1 \right )e^{-\Delta t_1/RC} [/latex] [latex]\left (1-\frac{1}{4} \right )=\left ( \frac{1}{2}+1 \right )e^{-\Delta t_1/RC} [/latex] [latex]\frac{3}{4}=\frac{3}{2}e^{-\Delta t_1/RC}[/latex] [latex] e^{\Delta t_1/RC}=2\;\;....(i) [/latex] In time [latex] t=\Delta t_2 [/latex] [latex]V_c=V_{LTP};  [/latex]   [latex]V_{initial}=V_{UTP}; [/latex]  [latex]V_{final}=-V_{sat} [/latex] [latex]V_{LTP}=-V_{sat}+(V_{UTP}+V_{sat})e^{-\Delta t_2/RC} [/latex] [latex]-\frac{V_{sat}}{2}=-V_{sat}+\left ( \frac{V_{sat}}{4}+V_{sat} \right )e^{-\Delta t_2/RC} [/latex] [latex]\left (1-\frac{1}{2} \right )V_{sat}=V_{sat}\left (1+ \frac{1}{4} \right )e^{-\Delta t_2/RC} [/latex] [latex]\frac{1}{2}= \frac{5}{4}e^{-\Delta t_2/RC} [/latex] [latex]e^{\Delta t_2/RC}=\frac{5}{2}\;\;....(ii)[/latex] From equation (i) and (ii), [latex]\frac{e^{\Delta t_1/RC}}{e^{\Delta t_2/RC}}[/latex] [latex]=e^{(\Delta t_1-\Delta t_2)/RC}[/latex] [latex]=\frac{2}{5/2}=\frac{4}{5}=0.8[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
This circuit is a stable multivibrator (or) free running oscillator.
When [latex]V_0=+V_{sat} [/latex]
[latex]V_{UPT}=V_{sat}\times \frac{1k\Omega }{1k\Omega +3k\Omega } = \frac{V_{sat}}{4} [/latex]
When, [latex] V_0=-V_{sat} [/latex]
[latex]V_{LTP}=V_{sat}\times \frac{1k\Omega }{1k\Omega +1k\Omega }=\frac{-V_{sat}}{2}[/latex]

[latex]V_c=V_{final}+(V_{inital}-V_{final})e^{-t/RC}[/latex]
In time [latex] t=\Delta t_1[/latex]
[latex] V_c=V_{UTP}; [/latex] [latex]V_{initial}=V_{LTP};[/latex] [latex]V_{final}=+V_{sat}[/latex]
[latex]V_{UTP}=V_{sat}+(V_{LTP}-V_{sat})e^{-\Delta t_1/RC} [/latex]
[latex]\frac{V_{sat}}{4}=V_{sat}+\left ( -\frac{V_{sat}}{2}-V_{sat} \right )e^{-\Delta t_1/RC} [/latex]
[latex]V_{sat}\left ( -1+\frac{1}{4} \right )=-V_{sat}\left ( \frac{1}{2}+1 \right )e^{-\Delta t_1/RC} [/latex]
[latex]\left (1-\frac{1}{4} \right )=\left ( \frac{1}{2}+1 \right )e^{-\Delta t_1/RC} [/latex]
[latex]\frac{3}{4}=\frac{3}{2}e^{-\Delta t_1/RC}[/latex]
[latex] e^{\Delta t_1/RC}=2\;\;....(i) [/latex]

In time [latex] t=\Delta t_2 [/latex]
[latex]V_c=V_{LTP}; [/latex] [latex]V_{initial}=V_{UTP}; [/latex] [latex]V_{final}=-V_{sat} [/latex]
[latex]V_{LTP}=-V_{sat}+(V_{UTP}+V_{sat})e^{-\Delta t_2/RC} [/latex]
[latex]-\frac{V_{sat}}{2}=-V_{sat}+\left ( \frac{V_{sat}}{4}+V_{sat} \right )e^{-\Delta t_2/RC} [/latex]
[latex]\left (1-\frac{1}{2} \right )V_{sat}=V_{sat}\left (1+ \frac{1}{4} \right )e^{-\Delta t_2/RC} [/latex]
[latex]\frac{1}{2}= \frac{5}{4}e^{-\Delta t_2/RC} [/latex]
[latex]e^{\Delta t_2/RC}=\frac{5}{2}\;\;....(ii)[/latex]
From equation (i) and (ii),
[latex]\frac{e^{\Delta t_1/RC}}{e^{\Delta t_2/RC}}[/latex]
[latex]=e^{(\Delta t_1-\Delta t_2)/RC}[/latex]
[latex]=\frac{2}{5/2}=\frac{4}{5}=0.8[/latex]

questions.question:
The SOP (sum of products) form of a Boolean function is [latex]\Sigma [/latex](0,1,3,7,11), where
inputs are A, B, C , D (A is MSB, and D is LSB). The equivalent minimized expression of the function is
questions.explanation: The 4 variable Boolean function is given in canonical sum of product form as, [latex]f(A,B,C,D)=\Sigma (0,1,3,7,11)[/latex] As the options are given in the simplified product of sum form, we first convert the given function in canonical product of sum form, as under [latex]f(A,B,C,D)=\Pi (2,4,5,6,8,9,10,12,13,14,15)[/latex] Now by plotting the above function on a 4 variable K-map (Maxterm map), we obtain the simplified expression of the function [latex]f=(\bar{B}+C)\cdot (\bar{A}+C)\cdot (\bar{A}+\bar{B})\cdot (\bar{C}+D)[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
The 4 variable Boolean function is given in canonical sum of product form as,
[latex]f(A,B,C,D)=\Sigma (0,1,3,7,11)[/latex]
As the options are given in the simplified product of sum form, we first convert the given function in canonical product of sum form, as under
[latex]f(A,B,C,D)=\Pi (2,4,5,6,8,9,10,12,13,14,15)[/latex]
Now by plotting the above function on a 4 variable K-map (Maxterm map), we obtain the simplified expression of the function

[latex]f=(\bar{B}+C)\cdot (\bar{A}+C)\cdot (\bar{A}+\bar{B})\cdot (\bar{C}+D)[/latex]

questions.question: A JK flip flop can be implemented by T flip-flops. Identify the correct implementation.
questions.explanation: To obtain a JK flip-flop from a T flip-flop, we first constuct the characteristic table of JK flip-flop, and then obtain the excitation values for the T flip-flop as shown below Now, assuming T to be an output, we solve it in terms of J, K, [latex]Q_n[/latex] inputs. This gives the defination of the logic to be applied on the T input. questions.explanation: Using Mason's gain fomlula, Transfer function, [latex]G(s)=\frac{C(s)}{U(s)}=\frac{\Sigma P_k\Delta _k}{\Delta } [/latex] Forward paths are: [latex]P_1=\frac{h_0}{s^2} ,\; P_2=\frac{h_1}{s} [/latex] Individual loops are: [latex] L_1=\frac{-a_1}{s} , \; L_2=\frac{-a_0}{s^2} [/latex] Non-touching loops=zero [latex] \therefore \;\;\Delta _1=1, [/latex] [latex]\;\;\;\; \Delta _2=1-\left ( \frac{-a_1}{s} \right ) =\left ( 1+\frac{a_1}{s} \right ) =\left ( \frac{s+a_1}{s} \right ) [/latex] [latex]\;\;\;\;\Delta =1-\left ( \frac{-a_1}{s}-\frac{a_0}{s^2} \right )=\frac{s^2+a_1s+a_0}{s^2} [/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\; G(s)=\frac{C(s)}{U(s)}=\frac{P_1\Delta _1+P_2\Delta _2}{\Delta } [/latex] [latex]\;\;\;\;=\frac{\left ( \frac{h_0}{s^2} \right )\times 1+\left ( \frac{h_1}{s} \right )\times \left ( \frac{s+a_1}{s} \right )}{\frac{s^2+a_1s+a_0}{s^2}} [/latex] [latex]\;\;\;=\left [ \frac{h_0+h_1(s+a_1)}{s^2+a_1s+a_0} \right ] [/latex] Given:  [latex] h_1=b_1 [/latex] and [latex]h_0=b_0-b_1a_1[/latex] Thus,  [latex] G(s)=\frac{(b_0-b_1a_1)+b_1(s+a_1)}{(s^2+a_1s+a_0)} [/latex] [latex]G(s)=\left ( \frac{b_1s+b_0}{s^2+a_1s+a_0} \right )[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Using Mason's gain fomlula,
Transfer function,
[latex]G(s)=\frac{C(s)}{U(s)}=\frac{\Sigma P_k\Delta _k}{\Delta } [/latex]
Forward paths are:
[latex]P_1=\frac{h_0}{s^2} ,\; P_2=\frac{h_1}{s} [/latex]
Individual loops are:
[latex] L_1=\frac{-a_1}{s} , \; L_2=\frac{-a_0}{s^2} [/latex]
Non-touching loops=zero
[latex] \therefore \;\;\Delta _1=1, [/latex]
[latex]\;\;\;\; \Delta _2=1-\left ( \frac{-a_1}{s} \right ) =\left ( 1+\frac{a_1}{s} \right ) =\left ( \frac{s+a_1}{s} \right ) [/latex]
[latex]\;\;\;\;\Delta =1-\left ( \frac{-a_1}{s}-\frac{a_0}{s^2} \right )=\frac{s^2+a_1s+a_0}{s^2} [/latex]
[latex]\therefore \;\; G(s)=\frac{C(s)}{U(s)}=\frac{P_1\Delta _1+P_2\Delta _2}{\Delta } [/latex]
[latex]\;\;\;\;=\frac{\left ( \frac{h_0}{s^2} \right )\times 1+\left ( \frac{h_1}{s} \right )\times \left ( \frac{s+a_1}{s} \right )}{\frac{s^2+a_1s+a_0}{s^2}} [/latex]
[latex]\;\;\;=\left [ \frac{h_0+h_1(s+a_1)}{s^2+a_1s+a_0} \right ] [/latex]
Given: [latex] h_1=b_1 [/latex] and [latex]h_0=b_0-b_1a_1[/latex]
Thus, [latex] G(s)=\frac{(b_0-b_1a_1)+b_1(s+a_1)}{(s^2+a_1s+a_0)} [/latex]
[latex]G(s)=\left ( \frac{b_1s+b_0}{s^2+a_1s+a_0} \right )[/latex]

The function [latex]f(x)=e^{x}-1[/latex] is to be solved using Newton-Raphson method. If the initial value of [latex]x_0[/latex] is taken as 1.0, then the absolute error observed at [latex]2^{nd}[/latex] iteration is _____.
questions.explanation: Given, [latex]f(x)=e^x-1[/latex] or, [latex]f(x_K)=e^{x_K}-1[/latex] and [latex]x_0=1[/latex] In Newton-Raphson method, we have [latex]\begin{aligned} x_{K+1}&=\left [ x_K-\frac{f(x_K)}{f'(x_K)} \right ] \\ x_1&= \left [ x_0- \frac{f(x_0)}{f'(x_0)}\right ]\;\;...(i)\\ \text{Now, } f(x_0)&=e^{x_0}-1=e^1-1=(e-1) \\ \text{and, } f'(x)&=e6x \\ \therefore \;\; f'(x_0) &=e^1=e \end{aligned}[/latex] Putting the values, we get: [latex]\begin{aligned} x_1&=\left [ 1-\frac{e-1}{e} \right ]=\left [ \frac{e-e+1}{e} \right ]=e^{-1}\\ \text{Also, }x_2&=\left [ x_1-\frac{f(x_1)}{f'(x_1)} \right ]\;\;...(ii)\\ \text{Now, }x_1&=\frac{1}{e}=e^{-1} \text{ and } f(x_1)=(e^{e^{-1}}-1)\\ f'(x_1)&=e^{e^{-1}} \end{aligned}[/latex] Putting the value, we get: [latex]\begin{aligned} x_2&=\left [ e^{-1}-\frac{(e^{e^{-1}}-1)}{e^{e^{-1}}} \right ]\\ &=\left [ e^{-1}-\frac{(e^{0.37}-1)}{e^{0.37}} \right ]=0.06 \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Given, [latex]f(x)=e^x-1[/latex]
or, [latex]f(x_K)=e^{x_K}-1[/latex] and [latex]x_0=1[/latex]
In Newton-Raphson method, we have
[latex]\begin{aligned} x_{K+1}&=\left [ x_K-\frac{f(x_K)}{f'(x_K)} \right ] \\ x_1&= \left [ x_0- \frac{f(x_0)}{f'(x_0)}\right ]\;\;...(i)\\ \text{Now, } f(x_0)&=e^{x_0}-1=e^1-1=(e-1) \\ \text{and, } f'(x)&=e6x \\ \therefore \;\; f'(x_0) &=e^1=e \end{aligned}[/latex]
Putting the values, we get:
[latex]\begin{aligned} x_1&=\left [ 1-\frac{e-1}{e} \right ]=\left [ \frac{e-e+1}{e} \right ]=e^{-1}\\ \text{Also, }x_2&=\left [ x_1-\frac{f(x_1)}{f'(x_1)} \right ]\;\;...(ii)\\ \text{Now, }x_1&=\frac{1}{e}=e^{-1} \text{ and } f(x_1)=(e^{e^{-1}}-1)\\ f'(x_1)&=e^{e^{-1}} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Putting the value, we get:
[latex]\begin{aligned} x_2&=\left [ e^{-1}-\frac{(e^{e^{-1}}-1)}{e^{e^{-1}}} \right ]\\ &=\left [ e^{-1}-\frac{(e^{0.37}-1)}{e^{0.37}} \right ]=0.06 \end{aligned}[/latex]

 4P_{e1}+2P_{h1}&=750W \\ 
 2P_{e1}+P_{h1}&=375 W\;\;...(iv) 
\end{aligned}[/latex] Solving equation (iii) and (iv), we get, [latex]
P_{e1}=62.5 W [/latex] and [latex] P_{h1}=250W[/latex] Thus, at 25 Hz, hysteresis loss = 250W and eddy current loss =62.5W

questions.question:
A separately excited 300 V DC shunt motor under no load runs at 900 rpm
drawing an armature current of 2 A. The armature resistance is 0.5 [latex]\Omega[/latex] and leakage inductance is 0.01 H. When loaded, the armature current is 15 A. Then, the speed in rpm is _____.
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Given,}\;\; V &= 300 \text{volt, no load speed} \\ &=900 \text{rpm, no load current}\\ I_{a_0}&=2A \\ &\therefore \; \text{No load induced emf}\\ E_{a_0}&=V-I_{a_0}R\\ &=300-2 \times 0.5\\ &=299 \text{volt}\\ \end{aligned}[/latex] Also, full load armature current, [latex]I_{a_f}=15A [/latex] [latex]\therefore[/latex] induced emf in armature at load, [latex]\begin{aligned} E_{a_f}&=V-I_{a_f}R_a \\ &= 300-15 \times 0.5\\ &= 292.5 \text{volt} \end{aligned} [/latex] Let the speed of motor during loaded condition be N. We know that: [latex]\begin{aligned} E_a &\propto \phi N \\ \text{or} \;\; E_a&\propto N\;\;(\phi =\text{constant}) \\ \therefore \; \frac{N}{N_0} &=\frac{E_{a_f}}{E_{a_0}} \\ N&= \frac{E_{a_f}}{E_{a_0}} N_0\\ &= \frac{292.5}{299} \times 900\\ N&=880.43 \text{rpm} \end{aligned}[/latex]

Also, full load armature current,
[latex]I_{a_f}=15A [/latex]
[latex]\therefore[/latex] induced emf in armature at load,
[latex]\begin{aligned} E_{a_f}&=V-I_{a_f}R_a \\ &= 300-15 \times 0.5\\ &= 292.5 \text{volt} \end{aligned} [/latex]
Let the speed of motor during loaded condition be N.
We know that:
[latex]\begin{aligned} E_a &\propto \phi N \\ \text{or} \;\; E_a&\propto N\;\;(\phi =\text{constant}) \\ \therefore \; \frac{N}{N_0} &=\frac{E_{a_f}}{E_{a_0}} \\ N&= \frac{E_{a_f}}{E_{a_0}} N_0\\ &= \frac{292.5}{299} \times 900\\ N&=880.43 \text{rpm} \end{aligned}[/latex]

and the shunt admittance is[latex](0.0+j5.0)\mu mho /km[/latex]. The magnitude of the series
